嘉靖二十年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖二十年三月初九日，少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書、翰林院學士臣嚴嵩等於奉天門奏為科舉事：會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士夏言等六十九員。為進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

特進光祿大夫、上柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士夏言〔丁丑進士〕。
光祿大夫、太子太保兼太子太傅、禮部尚書、武英殿大學士翟鑾〔乙丑進士〕。
光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、吏部尚書許讚〔丙辰進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Twentieth Year of Jiajing (1541)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the ninth day of the third month of the twentieth year of Jiajing, your servant Yan Song, Junior Guardian concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Academician of the Hanlin Academy, together with other officials, submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“The Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected 300 successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we propose appointing 69 officials as Readers and other officiating personnel, including Xia Yan, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall. Regarding the distinctions of status conferred upon metropolitan graduates, we respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao: the first class customarily comprises three candidates. The first receives rank 6b, and the second and third receive rank 7a; they are granted the designation ‘metropolitan graduate with honors’ (jinshi jidi). Those in the second class receive rank 7b and are granted ‘metropolitan graduate status’ (jinshi chushen). Those in the third class receive rank 8a and are granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate’ (tong jinshi chushen).”

The imperial rescript received was: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Xia Yan held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Special Advancement and Supreme Pillar of State. He served as Junior Preceptor concurrently as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.〕

Zhai Luan held the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. He served as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent concurrently as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.〕

Xu Zan held the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Pillar of State. He served as Junior Guardian concurrently as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the twentieth year of Jiajing (1541), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the nineteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial regalia at the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial proclaimed the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation, led by drums and music, out through the Left Chang’an Gate. After the proclamation had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the twentieth day of the third month…

On the twenty-second day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed on the first-place graduate, and paper currency on the metropolitan graduates.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status with honors.

Shen Kun 沈坤 was on the military register of Dahe Guard in Zhili, with ancestral origins in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture. A student of the Shanyang County school, he specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Bozai; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Hui, and his father Wei; his mother was née Yu. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Zeng, Yu, and Fang, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Sheng 潘晟 was on the civilian register of Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing). His courtesy name was Siming; he ranked tenth in family birth order and was aged twenty-five, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangzong, his grandfather Xianchao, and his father Risheng, an Instructor; his mother was née Shi. Both parents were still living. His elder brothers were Shi, Min, and Zui; his younger brothers were Jiong, Hao, Chen, Huang, and Jing. His wife was née He. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yifeng 林一鳳 was registered with the Longjiang Left Guard in Nanjing, with ancestral origins in Xiangfu County, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing). His courtesy name was Boyu; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zu, his grandfather Zong, and his father Zai; his mother was née Lin, and his stepmothers were née Zhou and née Gao. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Yilin, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Gao Yi 高儀 was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zixiang and ranked third in his family. He was twenty-five, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Fu, and his father Yue; his father's former wife was née Cao, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Lun, and his younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Zhong. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Fen 董份 was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yongjun and ranked first in his family. He was thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Huan, a tribute scholar; his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was living. He married a woman née Gu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Sheng 陳陞 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Jinfu and ranked twenty-eighth in his family. He was thirty, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lei was honorifically appointed Prefect and received successive posthumous honors culminating in Grand Master of the Palace and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left in a Provincial Administration Commission. His grandfather Tingjing was an Administrative Assistant and received successive posthumous honors culminating in the same rank and office. His father Huan was Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Right; his mother, née Hu, was granted the title Lady of Pure Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tan, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; Kai, an Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left; Chi, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination cohort; Jie; and Pei. His younger brothers were Ying, an Office Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Shu, a tribute scholar; Jin, an Imperial University student; Dian; Dian; Zhang; Yuan; and Shu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Shusheng, courtesy name Yuji, was registered in a military household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was apparently second in family birth order and aged thirty-three [?; the transcription is garbled], born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingxun; his grandfather, Piao 䕯 [?], held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father was Hu, and his mother was née Shen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Shufang and his younger brother Shude; his wife was née Li. He ranked fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Zhongcan, courtesy name Shicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was sixth in family birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Xiao, was a subprefectural Administrative Assistant; his father, Kui, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Min. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Boxiang and his younger brothers Shujun and Jixun; his wife was née Shao. He ranked third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Dongshan, courtesy name Shaoan, was registered in a civilian household in Shehong County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was seventh in family birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wengao; his grandfather was Ai; his father, Yingzong, held an honorary official title for longevity; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Enguang, an Imperial University student; Enshen; Cizhao; and Liangchen, a tribute student. His first wife was née Shan, and he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He ranked third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Ling, courtesy name Yuanchong, was registered in a scholar household in Jianyang County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in family birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xun, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather was Ge; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingyu and his younger brothers Peng, Kui, Cheng, Yong, and Shan; his wife was née Fan. He ranked seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Ne, courtesy name Minqing, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Wu County. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather and father are both recorded as Ke; his mother was née Lü. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Feng and Gao, and his younger brothers were Ci and Yan. He married a woman née Wu. He placed ninety-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yangzheng, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in a civilian household in Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-one, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhongrong; his grandfather, Heng, was a District Magistrate; and his father, Zhonghuai, was an Associate Prefect. His mother was née Dai, and his stepmother was née Lu. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Yangyu and Yanghui. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-fifth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Mo, courtesy name Rucheng, was registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi, and was a native of Datong County, Datong Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Hong, was a Ceremonial Escort; and his father, Sen, held the honorary title of Charitable Official. His mother was née Zhao, and his stepmother was née Liang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Xun. He married a woman née Xu. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Dagang, courtesy name Wanju, was registered in a military household in Binzhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather's name is transcribed as 𨾚 [?]; his father was Shirong; and his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Dajing and Dalun, and his younger brother was Daji. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Gong, courtesy name Suqing, was registered in a military household in Xinzheng County, Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Wang was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather Kui was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His father Shangxian was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and his mother, née Shen, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jie, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and Duo, a Ceremonial Usher; his younger brothers were Cao, Cai, and Zha. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Dawu, courtesy name Wencheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Kai was a Prefectural School Instructor, his grandfather Xiang a Post Station Master, and his father Ren. His mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dashao and Dazhang; his younger brothers were Dayuan, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Dashao, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year, Daqi, and Dayuan. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Cao. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Henian, courtesy name Weiren, was registered in a civilian household in Pinggu County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather Zhi was granted the titles of Gentleman of Literary Service and District Magistrate. His father Zhenru was an Assistant Prefect, promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master for Instruction. His mother, née Jin, was granted the title of Lady of Service. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Pengnian, Kunnian, and Songnian. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 112th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Tang, courtesy name Rusheng, was registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was thirty-ninth in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhixian; his grandfather Qiong was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works. His father Hu was a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Mao, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Cheng, was granted the same title. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Ke. He was betrothed to a woman née Lou and married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Sanle, courtesy name Ziyou, was registered in a military household of Henan Guard in Henan and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Luoyang County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was twenty-seven years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xing was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of the Palace, serving as Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather Quan was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor and additionally granted the same title and chief ministership. His father Han was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan, and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Gentleness. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sanjin, and his younger brothers were Sanpin, Sansheng, Sanxi, Sance, Sanhuai, and Sanchong. He married a woman née Ding. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Shiheng, courtesy name Sitong, was registered in a civilian household of Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-seven years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather was Yu, and his father was Ji, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shihong, and his younger brothers were Shi'an, Shining, Shihe (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Shichong, Shili, and Shiyi. He married a woman née Shao. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yan, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a civilian household of Cangxi County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked third among his brothers, and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather was Qing, and his father was Bogui; his mother was née Pu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were En and Rong. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zitao, courtesy name Zhongyu, was registered in a civilian household of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was twenty-seven years old, born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pa [?], his grandfather was Shizheng, and his father was Bangjun; his mother was née Yang. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His elder brother was Zirui, and his younger brothers were Jieyu [?], Zishun, Zizhong (a student admitted by virtue of an official's status), Zizhang, and Ziheng. He married a woman née Lin. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

何雲鴈〔貫浙江嚴州府分水縣匠籍，國子生，治《易經》，字時賓，行八，年三十，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖永鎮〔義官〕，祖璣，父瀚〔所吏目〕，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄雲龍，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第四十三名，會試第二十三名。
translation_en:
Sun Xu, registered in a military household in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a native of Shanghai County in Zhili and a student of the department school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Daogong. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Benhong; his grandfather, Peng, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Wanyi; his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Shao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji, and his younger brothers were Xu, Sheng, Zuan, Lun, and Shou. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Shizhong, registered in an artisan household in Qingfeng County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Daofu. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-seven and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Tingxun; his grandfather, Feng, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Yingkui; his mother was née Yan, and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jianzhong and Xiezhong. His wife was née Meng. He placed ninety-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Bingyi, registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Xingzhi. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Hao, and his mother was née Guo. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Bingjun and Bingchen, and his younger brother was Binglun. His wife was née Han. He placed seventy-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yunyan, registered in an artisan household in Fenshui County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shibin. Eighth in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Yongzhen, held an honorary title for public beneficence; his grandfather was Ji; his father, Han, was a Clerk of a sub-battalion office; and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Yunlong. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hong Chaoxuan, courtesy name Shunchen, was registered in a military household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanhao; his grandfather was Ruibin, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Qin; and his mother was née Ye. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brothers were Chaokui, Chaomian, and Chaosheng. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Cai. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Zhangfu, courtesy name Yuanli, was registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Keming; his grandfather was Shuzhen; his father was Tingqing; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shou and Tong; his younger brothers were Fu, Chun, Yi, and Ji. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Tingshi, courtesy name Ruming, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry, he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Biao; his grandfather was Cheng; his father was Ze; and his mother was née Xie. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Lian was a judge. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Bian, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tingzheng; his grandfather was Jing, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Qing; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers are listed as Yue, Yi, Shen, Huai, Yu, Xun, Heng (a ceremonial usher), Xing, Xin, Heng, Ti, and Cai [?: Heng appears twice, and twelve elder brothers are listed despite his stated rank of twelfth]. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Zhou, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daofu. Second in birth order, he was thirty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yong, posthumously appointed a Prefectural Judge; his grandfather was Qi; his father was Jun; his mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wanchun, and his younger brother was Dong. His wife was née Zhang. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Weiyi, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture. He was a county school student and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuzhong. First in birth order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Congjiang; his grandfather was Ruxin; his father was Qiye; and his mother was née Gu. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Weili and Weipi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Wenyao, registered in Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jiongfu. Second in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather was Zhang; and his father was Song, a Prefectural School Instructor. His father's former wife was née Qiu, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wenhuan, and his younger brothers were Wenwei, Wenbing, and Wenchi. His wife was née Sun; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiju, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhiqing. Fourth in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wenmei; his grandfather was Xingzheng; and his father was Yuanlong, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His father's former wife was née Xiong, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiqiu and Xisui. His wife was née Qin. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張斗寅〔貫湖廣常德府武陵縣民籍，府學附學生，治春秋，字子人，行一，年二十五，四月初八日生〕。曾祖鉁，祖紀，父廷英，母梁氏。具慶下，弟斗宿、斗樞、斗柄、斗正，娶彭氏。湖廣鄉試第六十三名，會試第九十七名。

周土〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州民籍，常熟縣人，國子生，治詩經，字厚卿，行十，年五十四，十月三十日生〕。曾祖濟，祖棠，父燁〔封監察御史〕，母王氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，兄塾〔訓導〕、坤〔知府〕、墨〔知府〕、塈、堂、墅、墼〔監生〕、在〔恭政〕、埜〔司務〕，弟堦、垔，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第四十一名，會試第三百名。

全賜〔貫廣西桂林府靈川縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字厚甫，行一，年三十一，九月初七日生〕。曾祖溥，祖存義，父瑞，母焦氏。具慶下，娶陸氏。廣西鄉試第十五名，會試第一百十九名。

尹祖懋〔貫江西吉安府永新縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字德卿，行四，年三十六，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖時裕〔壽官〕，祖謨〔贈翰林院編修，加贈刑部員外郎〕，父襄〔司經局洗馬〕，母史氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母郭氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄祖愛、祖憲〔訓術〕、祖慶，弟祖恕、祖寧、祖忠、祖志，娶高氏。江西鄉試第四十二名，會試第六十三名。
translation_en:
Zhang Douyin, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Ji, and his father Tingying; his mother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dousu, Doushu, Doubing, and Douzheng. He married a woman née Peng. He placed sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Tu, courtesy name Houqing, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changshu County. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked tenth among his brothers, was aged fifty-four, and was born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Tang, and his father Ye, who was granted the title of Investigating Censor; his mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shu, an Assistant Instructor; Kun, a Prefect; Mo, a Prefect; Ji; Tang; Shu; Ji, a student of the Imperial University; Zai, whose annotation reads gongzheng [?]; and Ye, an Office Manager. His younger brothers were Jie and Yin. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three-hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Quan Ci, courtesy name Houfu, was registered in a civilian household in Lingchuan County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Cunyi, and his father Rui; his mother was née Jiao. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fifteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and one-hundred-and-nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Zumao, courtesy name Deqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Shiyu held an honorary official title for longevity. His grandfather Mo was posthumously granted the title of Hanlin Academy Compiler and additionally that of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father Xiang was Librarian in the Classics and Documents Office. His mother, née Shi, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his stepmother, née Guo, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zu’ai, Zuxian, a Daoist Instructor, and Zuqing; his younger brothers were Zushu, Zuning, Zuzhong, and Zuzhi. He married a woman née Gao. He placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉夢元〔貫直隸保定府安州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯始，行一，年三十四，五月初三日生〕。曾祖珪〔歲貢生〕，祖表〔義官〕，父倫〔監生〕，母張氏。慈侍下，弟希元，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第十三名，會試第二百四十八名。

方治〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字進卿，行二，年二十八，八月二十四日生〕。曾祖天鐸，祖緒，父本洪，嫡母俞氏，生母張氏。具慶下，兄泮，弟沾，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第二十三名，會試第九名。

陰標〔貫直隸保定府容城縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字時準，行一，年二十九，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖枯〔巡檢〕，祖廷璽〔壽官〕，父從光，母何氏。重慶下，弟樽、梯、枓、椽，娶孫氏。順天府鄉試第一百十三名，會試第六十五名。

畢竟夔〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣，軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字叔元，行三十六，年四十一，一月初六日生〕。曾祖清，祖鑑，父偉卿，母方氏，繼母彭氏。永感下，兄竟英、竟恭〔府通判〕、竟芳，弟竟容〔兵部員外郎〕、竟立〔貢士〕、竟萬，娶程氏。江西鄉試第五名，會試第二百十二名。
translation_en:
Liu Mengyuan, registered in Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boshi. Ranked first among his brothers, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Biao, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his father was Lun, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xiyuan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Zhi, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jinqing. Ranked second among his brothers, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tianduo, his grandfather was Xu, and his father was Benhong. His legal mother was née Yu, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Pan and his younger brother was Zhan; his wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Biao, registered in Rongcheng County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shizhun. Ranked first among his brothers, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ku, a Police Chief; his grandfather was Tingxi, an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Congguang; and his mother was née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zun, Ti, Dou, and Chuan; his wife was née Sun. He placed 113th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bi Jingkui, registered in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shuyuan. Ranked thirty-sixth in his generation, he was aged forty-one and was born on the sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather was Jian, and his father was Weiqing. His mother was née Fang and his stepmother née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jingying, Jinggong, a Prefectural Assistant, and Jingfang. His younger brothers were Jingrong, a Vice Director in the Ministry of War; Jingli, a tribute scholar; and Jingwan. His wife was née Cheng. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陸杲〔貫錦衣衛官籍，浙江嘉興府平湖縣人，國子生，治禮記，字元晋，行四十二，年三十六，二月初九日生〕。曾祖珪〔義官〕，祖鋃〔知縣，累贈南京鴻臚寺卿，加贈都察院右副都御史〕，父淞〔南京光祿寺卿，贈都察院右副都御史〕，母王氏〔封太淑人〕。慈侍下，兄楷〔監生〕、東、杰〔工部右侍郎兼都察院右副都御史〕、棐〔貢士〕、樟、槩，弟集〔貢士〕、炳〔錦衣衛指揮使〕、煒〔中書舍人〕、標。娶徐氏，繼娶沈氏。順天府鄉試第四名，會試第八十一名。

translation_en:
Lu Gao, courtesy name Yuanjin, was registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked forty-second in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an honorary official for charitable service; his grandfather was Lang, a magistrate successively granted the posthumous titles of Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial at Nanjing and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his father was Song, Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing, posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. His mother, née Wang, was awarded the title of Grand Lady of Gentleness. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Kai, a National University student; Dong; Jie, Right Vice Minister of Works concurrently serving as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Fei, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Zhang; and Gai. His younger brothers were Ji, a tribute scholar; Bing, Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard; Wei, a Central Drafting Office Secretary; and Biao. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yi, courtesy name Zhangfu, was registered in a civilian household in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Dayou, his father Wei, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gun, and he married a woman née Xia. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Qiao, courtesy name Zongzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twenty-seventh in his family and was aged forty-six, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, a prefect; his grandfather was Pu, a prefectural school instructor; his father was Long; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhen, Zi, Gen, and Zhu. He married a woman née Che and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cai, courtesy name Yongqing, was registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minkuan, his grandfather Zhongzuo, his father Bi, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Quan and his younger brother Huan. He married a woman née Liang. He placed sixty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Ce: registered in a military household of Changsha Guard, Huguang, and a student of the Changsha County school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xishu. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Jun, his father Li, and his mother née Mao. His mother alone was still living. He married a woman née Duan. He placed sixty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jingxiang: registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Qiming. He ranked eleventh among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Wenxiu, his father Jing, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jingxing, Jingyun, and Jingyang. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Meizhong: registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jizhi. He ranked eighth among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yicheng, a department magistrate; his grandfather was Wentai, his father Jun, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shizhong and Yongzhong; his younger brothers were Daoming, a guard registrar, Jianzhong, Bingzhong, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Maozhong, Jizhong, and Daozhong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yiming: registered in an artisan household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanmo. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, an assistant instructor; his grandfather was Han and his father Guang. His father's former wife was née Jing, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yi'e and Yikui. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Wei, courtesy name Chaowen, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighth in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Ji, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and posthumously awarded that of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites. His father was Qin, a Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and his mother, née Zou, held the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tong, Commissioner of the Institute of Imperial Crafts, and Shou, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Xu, Ying, and Hui. His wife was née Qiu. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chongguang, courtesy name Tingxuan, was registered in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was forty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather was Wu, and his father was Lin, a county school Instructor. His mother was née Shen; his stepmothers were née Chang, Yue, and Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gengguang; his younger brothers were Enguang, Wenguang, Guoguang, Jinguang, and Guangguang. His wife was née Liu. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Zikai, courtesy name Benchu, was registered in the Wucheng Central Guard in a military household and was a native of Wuxi County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student (xiucai) of the Hanlin Academy specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lingshou, his grandfather was Bifan, and his father was Ming, a Company Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His mother was née Tao. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Tingzhang and Tingyu; his younger brother was Tingbi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Yugong, courtesy name Siji, was registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An attached student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-one years old, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather was Qin, a Vice Commissioner of a Salt Tax Office, and his father was Caida. His mother was née Yi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuliang, Yucong, Yuqiao, Yuzao (a county government school student), Yuzhi, Yuli, Yuxian, and Yujing. His wife was née Guo. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanhua; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Ying was a Registrar, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of Central Compliance (zhongshun dafu) and Assistant Administrator (zanzhi yin); his grandfather Feng was Salt Distribution Commissioner; and his father Ting was a Section Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted the title Gentleman for Attending to Duties. His father's former wife, née Xu, and his mother, née He, were each granted the title Lady of Repose. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brother was Luo and his younger brother Bin. He married a woman née Guo. He ranked thirtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Shen 黃深 was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was School Instructor in Wanzhou, Guangdong, and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shungong; he was seventh in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fifteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jue; his grandfather Wensheng was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Heng; and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dashu and his younger brother Yuan. He married a woman née Lin. He ranked eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fei Pang 費滂 was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyi, his grandfather Shen, his father Qin, and his mother née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Huan, a student of the Directorate of Education, Shen, and Zao. He married a woman née Li. He ranked sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Zhun 齊準 was registered under a military banner in the Chengdu Left Princely Guard, Sichuan, and was a native of Lintong County, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Pingfu; he was third in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zhixue, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Shikuan; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongren and Zhongrang; his younger brothers were Dou, Fu, Zhuo, Gao, Qian, and Shen. He married a woman née Yin. He ranked forty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

萬士和〔貫直隸常州府宜興縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字思節，行六，年二十六，十月十三日生〕。曾祖政，祖璵，父吉〔訓導〕，母李氏。具慶下，兄士弘、士亨〔同科進士〕、士安、士寧，弟士完、士吉、士宜，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第九名，會試第一百七名。

林大章〔貫福建福州府閩縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字章之，行三，年三十二，九月初一日生〕。曾祖均善，祖祈，父文喬，母李氏。重慶下，兄崇義，弟大經〔監生〕、大新、大資、大彥、大鼎、大叙、大有，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十五名，會試第一百三十七名。
translation_en:
Yi Zhonghe, registered in a military household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Tianjue; his father was Lun; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongli, Zhongfu (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Zhongdao, and Zhongyao. His wife was née Du. He placed sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hongfan, registered in an artisan household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiqing; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Wan; his father was Jingxiang; and his mother was née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Hongmeng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year. His wife was née Wu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Shihe, registered in a civilian household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Sijie; he ranked sixth in family birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Ji, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shihong, Shiheng (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year), Shi’an, and Shining; his younger brothers were Shiwan, Shiji, and Shiyi. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Dazhang, registered in a military household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhangzhi; he ranked third in family birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junshan; his grandfather was Qi; his father was Wenqiao; and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Chongyi; his younger brothers were Dajing (a student of the National University), Daxin, Dazi, Dayan, Dading, Daxu, and Dayou. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shifan 陳時範, courtesy name Fuchou, was registered in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather, Changchao, received the honorary title of Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; his father, Wenpei, served as acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His mother, née Xie, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shijian and Shidao, and his wife was née Dai. He placed twenty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hongmeng 陳洪濛, courtesy name Yuanqing, was registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household. An additional student of the county government school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Chong, his father Jingxiang, and his mother née Huang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Hongfan became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the same examination cohort. His wife was née Han. He placed sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jiong 李泂, courtesy name Boyuan, was registered in Laiyang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather, Min, was a County Vice Magistrate who received successive posthumous honors culminating in the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father, Duo, was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Zhao, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Fang and Zhi. His wife was née Sun, and he subsequently married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yan 王言, courtesy name Zida, was registered in Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, in a banner household and was a native of Zhaoyuan County. A student of the Penglai County government school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Zhen, his father Ao, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Sun. He placed seventy-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃顯〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字仁叔，行二，年四十四，九月十一日生〕。曾祖本，祖璲，父通，母吳氏。慈侍下，兄顥，弟頤，娶林氏。廣東鄉試第七十四名，會試第二十九名。
translation_en:
Yin Mai, registered in a military household of the Nanjing Rear Guard’s Right Guard and originally from Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shixun, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Mian, and his father Feng; his father’s former wife was née Ma, his mother née Qian, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qian (Assistant Instructor) and Xuan, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhengrong, registered in a military household in Ningyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dehui, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shangzhi, his grandfather Yingzhen, his father Keqin, and his mother née Ji. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhengse; his wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wife née Cao. He placed sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Guobin, registered in a banner household of Dongpingshan Guard and originally from Jinjiang County, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Sijing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Yu (a student of the Directorate of Education), his father Tianxi (Assistant Instructor), and his mother née Hao. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Guoen (tribute scholar, gongshi), and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xian, registered in a military household in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Renshu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ben, his grandfather Sui, his father Tong, and his mother née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Hao, his younger brother Yi, and his wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張鶚翼〔貫直隸松江府上海縣竈籍，國子生，治易經，字習之，行二，年四十三，七月二十五日生〕。曾祖昱，祖澤，父錫，前母高氏，母朱氏。永感下，兄鵬翼，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第二百八十一名。

尹燾〔貫浙江衢州府龍游縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字明溥，行三十九，年三十四，八月十二日生〕。曾祖汝漲，祖元𤪌，父蒙，母周氏。具慶下，兄寬、濟、勳、照〔貢士〕、煦，弟烈、然、繼善，娶余氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第一百五十三名。

金翮〔貫浙江温州府樂清縣竈籍，國子生，治詩經，字思振，行二，年三十三，五月初七日生〕。曾祖琯，祖𡌨，父絾，母嚴氏。慈侍下，兄澳，弟策，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百五十四名。
translation_en:
Li Qian, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zi’an, he ranked sixth in family order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong, his grandfather Xuanzheng, his father Suxin, and his mother née Fan; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kui, Dao, Xuan, and Feng, and his younger brothers Ti, Tong, Shu, Di, Xian, Xun, Yu, Dao, and Yun; his wife was née Qin. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Eyi, registered in a salt-producing household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xizhi, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Ze, and his father Xi; his father’s former wife was née Gao, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Pengyi, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Tao, registered in a civilian household in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingpu, he ranked thirty-ninth in family order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ruzhang, his grandfather Yuanqi (元𤪌) [?], his father Meng, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kuan, Ji, Xun, Zhao (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and Xu, and his younger brothers Lie, Ran, and Jishan; his wife was née Yu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin He, registered in a salt-producing household in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Sizhen, he ranked second in family order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Guan, his grandfather Pi (𡌨) [?], his father Cheng, and his mother née Yan; his father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ao, his younger brother Ce, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Nanjin, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tiqian. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daping, his grandfather Hong, and his father 𣠄 [reading uncertain]; his mother was née Qi and his stepmother née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nanzhen and Nanheng, and his wife was née Peng. He placed sixty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Jin, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jiqing. Fifth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Suiqi, a Registrar; his grandfather was Qikuang, a Clerk; his father was Tianzuo, and his mother was née Ou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Kejiu, Keda (a tribute scholar), Ying [?], Han (an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial), and Lan; his younger brothers were Chao, Jiang, and Hao. His wife was née He. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shan, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and served as Instructor at Quanzhou, Guangxi. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jichu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuxi, his grandfather Houju, and his father Lisheng; his mother was née Huo. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Jie and Xian, and his wife was née Li. He placed ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Tianshou, registered in Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to an artisan household and was originally from Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an Imperial University student and specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Pingfu. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Yu, and his father Feng; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Tianfu, Vice Commissioner of the Seal Casting Office, and Tianlu. His wife was née Lu. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

齊傑〔貫直隸安慶府桐城縣，軍匠籍，縣學生，治詩經，字士庸，行二，年四十二，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖良佐，祖可道，父秀，母喬氏。永感下，兄仁，弟儷、邁、述〔監生〕、遇〔貢士〕，娶潘氏。應天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第二百九十二名。

朱乾亨〔貫武驤左衛，軍籍，直隸徐州人，國子生，治易經，字子貞，行一，年二十九，四月十五日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖明，父華，前母宋氏，母劉氏。永感下，娶李氏，繼娶方氏、邵氏。順天府鄉試第二十六名，會試第三十七名。

李台〔貫湖廣荊州府公安縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字星伯，行一，年三十九，七月二十一日生〕。曾祖廣，祖珂，父大本〔知縣〕，母伍氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，弟右、若，娶葉氏，繼娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第六名，會試第二百九十三名。
translation_en:
Liu Jian, courtesy name Ruzhao, was registered in a civilian household in Anping County, Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili). A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, a tribute student; his grandfather was Shu, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan); his father was Yixiao, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Yin, and Xuan. His wife was née Yao. He ranked 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Jie, courtesy name Shiyong, was registered in a military artisan household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangzuo; his grandfather was Kedao; his father was Xiu, and his mother was née Qiao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ren; his younger brothers were Li, Mai, Shu, an Imperial University student, and Yu, a tribute student. His wife was née Pan. He ranked 102nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Qianheng, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered in a military household of the Wuxiang Left Guard and was a native of Xuzhou, Zhili. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Hua. His father's former wife was née Song, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married women née Fang and née Shao. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tai, courtesy name Xingbo, was registered in a military household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather was Ke; his father was Daben, a district magistrate; his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were You and Ruo. His wife was née Ye; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He ranked sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jue 王覺 was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Shixian and ranked fourth among his brothers. He was fifty years old, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Yin, and father, Jin, both held honorary official status awarded for public beneficence. His mother was née Pan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xue, Director of Sacrifices, and Ju, an Imperial University student; his younger brother Yu was also an Imperial University student. His wife was née Xu. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan 章煥 was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shuhui and ranked twenty-ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-four years old, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Bi, his father Se, and his mother née He. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Lian. His wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 306th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qia 張洽 was registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zide and ranked thirteenth among his brothers. He was twenty-six years old [?; the transcription omits the character introducing his age], born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Peng, had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under an applicable regulation. His grandfather, Hui, was Medical Officer and received the honorary title of Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His father, Yingyou, was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bo, Can, Ji, Han (Bureau Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice), Ting, Yu (a tribute scholar), and Lan. His younger brothers were Chun (followed by the annotation “all Imperial University students,” whose scope is uncertain [?]), Hu, Jiang, Lian, Hong, Zi, Zhou, Shu, Bin, Zhan, and Lin. His wife was née Lai. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Danian 陶大年 was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Changqing and ranked twelfth among his brothers. He was twenty-nine years old, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zao, was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Left Vice Minister of War, and concurrent Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Shi, was Registrar of Shouning County; his father, Shiqi, was Steward of Provisions; and his mother was née Shen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dahua, an Imperial University student, and Daquan. His wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Shihong 董士弘, courtesy name Tiren, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in family order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Shangbin, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father, Shao, was a county magistrate. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother survived. His younger brothers were Shiyi and Shiqi, both students of the Directorate of Education, Shi’an, and Shining. His wife was née Tang. He placed 126th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 59th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fumin 王撫民, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in a military household of the Right Battalion of Zhending Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Qingyuan County, Shanxi. A student of the Zhending Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, his grandfather Lian, his father You, and his mother née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yumin, Xinmin, and Zemin. His wife was née Ren. He placed 76th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gang 徐綱, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was fourth in family order, aged forty-two, and born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Han, his grandfather Hong, his father Bi, and his mother née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother survived. His elder brothers were Ji and Shou, and his younger brother was Chun. His wife was née Zhang. He placed 44th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chonggu 王崇古, courtesy name Xuefu, was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. An added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was sixth in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Menghua, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather, Xin, was a school instructor and was posthumously granted the title of Secretariat Drafter. His father was Yao, his mother née Sun, and his stepmother née Meng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chongren, Chongyi, Chongdao, a student of the Directorate of Education, Chongzu, and Chongzhi; his younger brothers were Chongshu, Chongdian, Chongxun, and Chongjiao. His wife was née Zhang. He placed tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hou Yue, courtesy name Yifu, was from Dong’e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was registered in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sui, his grandfather Youde, and his father Quan; his mother was née Gong. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Qin and his younger brother Biao. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wu, courtesy name Sizhi, was from Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was registered in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an Instructor; his grandfather was Xicheng, and his father Zewu; his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Gui. He married a woman née Cheng. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Weiyi, courtesy name Jifu, was from Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was registered in a civilian household. A supplementary student at the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather You, and his father Gao; his mother was née Hu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brother was Weixin. He married a woman née Fan. He placed twentieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
