translation_en:
Third Class: 205 men, granted the status of associate metropolitan graduate (tong jinshi chushen).

Zhou Ao, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jinglu; he ranked twenty-eighth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Pu, his father Yu, and his mother née Zhan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, Wei, Cheng, and Xiang; his younger brothers were Xue, Li, Song, Jiao, Yi, Mu, Chun, and Shan [the last three names are uncertain: 木椿山, ?]. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yanghao, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Bochong; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Yi, and his father Fan, who had been granted the titles of Grand Master for Governmental Service and Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Ye, had been granted the title of Grand Lady of Suitability. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Yangzheng, a Prefect, and Yangxian; his younger brothers were Yangsu and Yanglian. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Wangdao, registered in a civilian household in Hua County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-four years old, born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Song, who held an honorary official title bestowed for longevity; his grandfather was Fu, his father Xu, and his mother née Zhao. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Xian; his younger brothers were Wanghua and Shandao. He married a woman née Shi. He placed ninety-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Mian, courtesy name Shujing, was from Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and registered in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yonggang; his grandfather, Shicong; his father, Quan; and his mother, née Jiang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bing, Chao, and Xu. His wife was née Xu. He placed twentieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Zhida, courtesy name Zidi, was from Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a salt-producing household. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Dehua, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Huan, was a County Magistrate and formerly a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Yan, and his mother was née Tao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jin, Zhixiao, and Zhiren; his younger brothers were Zhiqian, Zhigao, Zhide, Zhiming, Zhizhong, Zhishan, and Zhiyuan. His wife was née Qiao; he subsequently married a woman née Xie. He placed 122nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yao, courtesy name Runfu, was from Zuocheng County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, and registered in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Shen, was a Prison Warden; and his father, Ji, was an Assistant Magistrate of a subprefecture. His legal mother was née Li, his stepmother née Zhang, and his birth mother née Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Kun. His wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Liangfu, courtesy name Shupi, was from Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a salt-producing household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Quan; and his father, Xiao, who held an honorary official title granted for longevity. His legal mother was née Cao and his birth mother née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Liangzuo, an Imperial University student, and Liangjun, an annual tribute student. His wife was née Song. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

治詩經字子喬行一年二十八五月十八日生
曾祖勝　祖智　父詩　母金氏

鄢懋卿〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字景修，行六，年三十四，正月三十日生〕。曾祖承之〔義官〕，祖謐〔壽官〕，父高〔知縣〕，母周氏，繼母謝氏、楊氏。嚴侍下，兄愚卿，弟愈卿、悊卿、憲卿、慤卿，娶王氏。江西鄉試第十一名，會試第一百十八名。

李時濟〔貫山東青州府壽光縣，軍籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字伯舟，行一，年三十，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖隨，祖海〔散官〕，父鏞〔縣丞〕，母馬氏，繼母劉氏。具慶下，弟時漸、時晉、時升、時臨，娶張氏。山東鄉試第十五名，會試第四十三名。

陳松〔貫直隸河間府青縣，屯種軍籍，河南裕州葉縣縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字子喬，行一，年二十八，五月十八日生〕。曾祖勝，祖智，父詩，母金氏。重慶下，弟梅，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第七十五名，會試第二百二十五名。
translation_en:
Lu Keyou, registered in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zizheng. He ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Yunhan, a Prefectural School Instructor; and his father was Yin. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kezun, and his younger brothers were Kelü, Keyuan, and Keda. His wife was née Hu. He placed forty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Maoqing, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingxiu. He ranked sixth among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chengzhi, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his grandfather was Mi, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Gao, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Zhou, and his stepmothers were née Xie and née Yang. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Yuqing (愚卿), and his younger brothers were Yuqing (愈卿), Zheqing, Xianqing, and Queqing. His wife was née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiji, registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bozhou. He ranked first among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sui; his grandfather was Hai, a prestige official; and his father was Yong, a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Ma, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shijian, Shijin, Shisheng, and Shilin. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Song, registered in Qing County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military farming household and was an added student at the county school of Ye County, Yu Subprefecture, Henan. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziqiao. He ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Zhi; and his father was Shi. His mother was née Jin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Mei, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Long, registered in a civilian household in Fenshui County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shijia, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gongmian, his grandfather Jie, and his father Mi; his mother was née Fang and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zhong, Huan, Cong, and Zuan, and his younger brothers Po, Jue, and Lu; his wife was née Cong. He placed eighteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yingce, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junyong, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, honorarily appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Zhen, posthumously appointed County Magistrate; and his father was Zhang, an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife, née Ke, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his mother, née Lin, was granted the same title. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingxiang, Yingchen, Yingxing (a metropolitan examination graduate, gongshi), Yingyou, and Yingzhen; his wife was née Lin. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Bi, registered in a civilian household in Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shizhong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Youliang, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Sheng, his father Yunjing, and his mother née Nan. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xiu, and his younger brothers were Wu and Yun; his wife was née Cao. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Sizhong, registered in a military household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiaofu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather was Wenmao, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Rong, an Unranked Assistant; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Sichen and his younger brother Sishu; his wife was née Jing. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Xueliu, registered in Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongwen. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, a county Registrar; his grandfather was Yuan; his father was Xiang, a prefectural Clerk; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xuehan, and his younger brothers were Xue’ou, Xuesu, Xuezhou, Xuezhao, and Xuezeng. His wife was née Sun. He placed eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Cheng, registered in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xianqing. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather was Cong; his father was Qin; his mother was née Mao; and his stepmothers were née Cheng and née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yingzhou, and his wife was née Gao. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shen, registered in Wuqing County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zijin. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenxing; his grandfather was Yan; his father was Jingtang; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Endi [?], Jing, and Ji, and his younger brothers were Wei, Chun, and Shou. His wife was née Sun. He placed 109th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Bingde, registered in Puzhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Xinjian County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xingzhi. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liyuan; his grandfather was Bocan; his father was Shigang; and his mother was née Lei. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bingzhe, and his wife was née Li. He placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

王顯忠〔貫順天府覇州保定縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字元孝，行二，年二十七，閏四月二十四日生〕。曾祖興，祖宗〔倉副使，贈知縣，加贈奉政大夫、應天府治中〕，父誥〔奉政大夫、應天府治中〕，前母徐氏〔贈宜人〕，母徐氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄尚賓〔義官〕、尚忠〔七品散官〕、尚賢〔聽選官〕、輗，弟軒，娶任氏。順天府鄉試第七十九名，會試第一百十六名。

梁汝璧〔貫四川重慶府江津縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字應文，行二，年三十一，三月十五日生〕。曾祖楨，祖尚用，父佐，母周氏。具慶下，兄汝奎，娶袁氏。四川鄉試第五十二名，會試第二百七十三名。
translation_en:
Cui Yilian 崔一濂 was registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xuezhou; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather An, and his father Shijie; his mother was née Lao. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Yihan. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Guan. He placed sixty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chongjian 王崇儉 was registered in a civilian household in Cao County, Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shudu; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was fifty-two years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Dao and grandfather Lan were both posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief. His father Xun was Right Vice Censor-in-chief in the Censorate. His father's former wives, née Li and née Kong, were both posthumously granted the title of Lady of Virtue (shuren). His mother, née Huang, was granted the title of Lady of Respect (gongren) and posthumously that of Lady of Virtue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chongru, a District Magistrate; Chongren, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Chongwen, Right Vice Censor-in-chief in the Censorate; Chongxian, Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing; Chongrang, a Battalion Commander; and Chongyou, an Office Deputy in the Court of Imperial Entertainments. His younger brother was Chongye. He married a woman née Li. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xianzhong 王顯忠 was registered in an artisan household in Baoding County, Ba Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanxiao; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xing. His grandfather Zong was a Vice Director of a Granary, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate and additionally those of Grand Master for Governance and Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His father Gao was Grand Master for Governance and Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His father's former wife, née Xu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren); his mother, also née Xu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shangbin, an honorary official; Shangzhong, a seventh-rank titular official; Shangxian, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Ni. His younger brother was Xuan. He married a woman née Ren. He placed seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Rubi 梁汝璧 was registered in a civilian household in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county government student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yingwen; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fifteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Shangyong, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rukui. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed fifty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ma Zhongying, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a commoner household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Junchu. Third in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Zhang, his father Fengle, and his mother née Fu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yingfu and Zhongmeng, and his younger brothers Zhongyou, Zhongcun, and Zhonghan. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed fiftieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhi, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhiqing. First in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhao, his grandfather Yu, his father Sizhong, and his mother née Yan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Fujue. He married a woman née Liang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shixing, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a commoner household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shaoxie. First in birth order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Cong, his father Wenshao, his mother née Fei, and his stepmother née Zhong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shiyu, Shifeng, Shiliang, Shichun, and Shijin. He married a woman née Gong. He placed sixty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Lüxiang, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a commoner household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zixuan. First in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather Pu held prestige rank; and his father Yao was an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang. His father's former wife was née Zhang, his mother née Yang, and his stepmother née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Lüzhong, Lühe, and Lüdao. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Qile, courtesy name Weihe, was from Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a military household. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked 137th in family order and was aged thirty, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chong, his grandfather Rui, and his father Mian; his father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Shi. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Qili, and his wife was née Wu. He placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hua Shunqin, courtesy name Shuyu, was from Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth in family order and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Sichun and grandfather Kai both held honorary longevity titles; his father was En, and his mother was née Zou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Haoqin and Yaoqin, the latter a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brother was Wenqin, and his wife was née Qian. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Ruideng, courtesy name Hezhong, was from Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and registered in a civilian household. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Hao held an honorary title for charitable service; his grandfather was Kai, his father Yin, and his mother née Zhu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ruicheng, Ruiming, Ruiqian, and Ruilong, and his wife was née Zha. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Fengshi, courtesy name Zhaoxing, was from Jiayu County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, and registered in a civilian household. An supplementary student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in family order and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Mengding held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather was Chong, his father Heng, and his mother née Kong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fengyuan, Fengji, and Fengyin, and his wife was née Zhou. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Weichi, courtesy name Guoxiang, was registered in a civilian household in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chu, his grandfather Peizhi, his father Hua, and his mother née Xu; both parents were living, his wife was née Pan, and he ranked first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Bixiao, courtesy name Chunqing, was registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Xu, a prefect; his father was Lü, and his mother née Mao; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Biliang, a tribute scholar and Directorate student, B敬 (Bijing), a county vice magistrate, Zhi, a prefect, Biyi, and Bishun, his younger brothers were Bili, Bihong, Bishu, Bideng, Bifang, Bida, and Biyong, his wife was née Sun, and he ranked eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Liang, courtesy name Ziyin, was registered in a military household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; he was tenth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the sixth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhuang, his grandfather Zongxun, his father Mengping, his legal mother née Sun, and his birth mother née Du; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brothers were Wei, Pou, Bo, Bao, Gun, Chong, Mao, Biao, and Yan, his wife was née Lü, and he ranked eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Duanmeng, courtesy name Yueqi, was registered in a civilian household in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kun, his grandfather Tingguo, granted the title of Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy, his father Yucheng, a Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy, his mother née Zheng, granted the title of Lady (ruren), and his stepmother née Fan; his father was living and his mother deceased, his younger brothers were Duanben, Duansheng, Duanjin, Duanjian, and Duandun, his wife was née Yao, and he ranked seventy-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Yuan, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Daben. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather De, his father Zhen, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hong 澋, Ye, Si, and Lai; his wife was née Han. He placed forty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Shangjian, registered in Changyi County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanjing. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the eleventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather Guan was a Judge; his father Shiju was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Shangkuan, Shanggong, Shangde, and Shangqing; his wife was née Sun. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xicheng, registered in Xiangshan County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and served as Instructor at the county school of Shouzhang, Shandong. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Daofu. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Mengchu was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather Shangxian was an Assistant Instructor; his father Zhang was a Subprefectural School Instructor; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu 黼, Wenhao, and Fu 黻. He married a woman née Dong and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Shilin, registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruji. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fangchang, his grandfather Zhongji, and his father Guikang, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenxiao, Wenzheng, and Wenche; his younger brothers were Wenchi and Wenzhuang. His wife was née Hu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

魯佩〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字德夫，行十，年三十八，十一月二十七日生〕。曾祖崇獻〔七品散官〕，祖時諒，父昂〔縣丞〕，母熊氏。嚴侍下，弟仕、脩、伸，娶潘氏，繼娶衛氏、劉氏。江西鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百八十三名。

陳九德〔貫直隸真定府欒城縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字吉夫，行五，年三十二，二月初一日生〕。曾祖貴，祖正〔巡檢〕，父鸞〔訓導〕，母許氏，繼母張氏。重慶下，兄九功、九韶、九疇、九皐，弟存仁、存禮，娶魏氏。順天府鄉試第八十九名，會試第九十二名。

吳崇文〔貫河南汝寧府光山縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字質夫，行一，年二十七，二月初九日生〕。曾祖珏〔監生〕，祖九岐〔府檢校〕，父漢，母劉氏。具慶下，弟崇獻、崇道，娶夏氏。河南鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百四名。

王忲〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州，軍籍，崑山縣人，國子生，治易經，字民應，行十一，年三十五，五月初四日生〕。曾祖琳〔贈通議大夫兵部右侍郎〕，祖輅〔累贈通議大夫兵部右侍郎〕，父倬〔通議大夫兵部右侍郎〕，前母陳氏〔贈淑人〕、陳氏〔贈孺人〕，母陳氏〔封淑人〕。永感下，兄愷、惇〔貢士贈禮部主事〕、怡、憬〔知縣〕、愔〔淳安知縣〕、恬〔監生〕、懽〔典膳〕、恪〔監生〕、禎〔監生〕、忱，娶郁氏。應天府鄉試第六十二名，會試第一百六十六名。
translation_en:
Lu Pei, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked tenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongxian, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather was Shiliang; his father was Ang, a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née Xiong. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shi, Xiu, and Shen. He married a woman née Pan, then successively women née Wei and Liu. He placed sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiude, registered in Luancheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jifu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Zheng, a Police Chief; his father was Luan, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Xu; and his stepmother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jiugong, Jiushao, Jiuchou, and Jiugao; his younger brothers were Cunren and Cunli. He married a woman née Wei. He placed eighty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chongwen, registered in Guangshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jue, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Jiuqi, a Prefectural Proofreader; his father was Han; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chongxian and Chongdao. He married a woman née Xia. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tai, registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a military household and was a native of Kunshan County. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Minying; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Lin was posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War; his grandfather Lu received these same titles through successive posthumous grants; and his father Zhuo held these titles. His father's former wives were a woman née Chen, posthumously titled Lady of Virtue, and another woman née Chen, posthumously titled Lady; his mother, also née Chen, was invested with the title Lady of Virtue. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kai; Dun, a tribute scholar posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; Yi; Jing, a County Magistrate; Yin, Magistrate of Chun'an County; Tian, an Imperial University student; Huan, a Director of Delicacies; Ke, an Imperial University student; Zhen, an Imperial University student; and Chen. He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

方廉〔貫浙江杭州府新城縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字以清，行十，年二十九，正月十一日生〕。曾祖鏞〔醫學訓科〕，祖源〔教諭〕，父模，前母羅氏，母錢氏，繼母凌氏。具慶下，兄暉、煥、煉，弟勳、炬、炘。娶羅氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第一百二名。

何孟倫〔貫廣東廣州府新會縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字慎明，行一，年三十六，七月初五日生〕。曾祖真宗，祖洋，父章，母吳氏，繼母黃氏。重慶下，弟仲倫、季倫。娶余氏。廣東鄉試第二十八名，會試第三名。
translation_en:
Zhou Yao, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingpei; he ranked eighth in his family and was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benxue; his grandfather was Fuchen; and his father was Zongyuan, an honorary official for longevity. His father's former wife was née Yin, and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan, Lian, Jie (a sacrificial attendant), Qiong, Qi, Zhang, and Gong; his younger brothers were Dai, Rong, Chong, Pei, Lang, Xuan, Xuan, Zhi, and Cui. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zheng, registered in a civilian household in Yihuang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kejing; he ranked tenth in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengkuan; his grandfather was Shouying, an honorary official for longevity; and his father was Yi, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Cheng. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Jian (a subprefectural Clerk), Yong, E, Gao (an Instructor), Yue, and Ming (a garrison Steward of Provisions [?]); his younger brothers were Jun and Yu. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Wei. He placed sixty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Lian, registered in a civilian household in Xincheng County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiqing; he ranked tenth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, a Medical Instructor; his grandfather was Yuan, an Instructor; and his father was Mo. His father's former wife was née Luo, his mother was née Qian, and his stepmother was née Ling. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hui, Huan, and Lian; his younger brothers were Xun, Ju, and Xin. He married a woman née Luo. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Menglun, registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shenming; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhenzong; his grandfather was Yang; and his father was Zhang. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Huang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhonglun and Jilun. He married a woman née Yu. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Shu 李庶, registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jiqing; he ranked ninth among his brothers and male cousins and was twenty-seven sui, born on the third day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Kuang; his grandfather, Run, was a provincial graduate who served as acting Instructor; and his father was Fu. His father's former wife was née Xie, and his mother was née Shi. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Tun, Qiao, Mo, Jishou, Chun, and Jicheng [?]; Jicheng was awaiting selection for official appointment. His younger brothers are listed as Gao, Zhe, Yan, Lie, and Shu [?—the last repeats his own name]. He married a woman née Zeng. He placed seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Liangchen 郝良臣, registered in a military household in Xiangyuan County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingjin; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was forty sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Wenyi, and his father Zhen. His mother was née Fu, and his stepmother was née Xu. His parents were deceased. He married a woman née Cui. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Wei 鈕緯, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongwen; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Da, was posthumously appointed Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather, Qing, was Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father was Tingxin, and his mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Xu and Yi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shun 楊順, registered in a military household of the Dezhou Left Guard in the Metropolitan Region and originally from Wendeng County, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zibei; he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-one sui, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Hao, and his father Bingzhong. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xian, and his younger brothers were Yong and Jie. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張祥〔貫南京錦衣衛官籍，直隸常州府武進縣人，山東泗水縣學訓導，治易經，字元吉，行二，年四十六，六月二十一日生〕。曾祖鎬〔武略將軍、中舍人〕，祖吉〔錦衣衛正千戶〕，父春〔錦衣衛正千戶〕，前母劉氏、李氏，母唐氏〔封宜人〕，繼母馬氏、彭氏。慈侍下，兄瑞〔錦衣衛正千戶〕，弟祉，娶吳氏。山東鄉試第四十七名，會試第二百五十七名。
translation_en:
Zhang Mu, courtesy name Shunchen, was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and served as Instructor at the county school of Lin County, Shanxi. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Gao, and his father Tingrui; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Min, Xi (an Instructor), and Zheng. His wife was née Mao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Cong, courtesy name Yuzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged forty-three, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Neng, and his father Kuan (an honorary official for longevity); his father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Xiu (a medical official). His wife was née Wu. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Maoqing, courtesy name Shiyu, was registered in a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and served as Instructor at the county school of Xianju County, Zhejiang. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty-five, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiao, his grandfather Zhongxiu, and his father Jili; his mother was née Lin, and his stepmother was née He. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Diaoqing, Jieqing, Yiqing, Jianqing, and Juqing. His wife was née Huang; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiang, courtesy name Yuanji, was registered in an officer household of the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. He served as Assistant Instructor at the county school of Sishui County, Shandong. He specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged forty-six, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao (General of Military Strategy and Central Secretary [?]); his grandfather Ji and father Chun were both Battalion Commanders in the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His father's former wives were née Liu and née Li; his mother was née Tang (invested with the title Lady of Suitability), and his stepmothers were née Ma and née Peng. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Rui (a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard), and his younger brother was Zhi. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Meizhong, registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruwen, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Shu, his father Di, and his mother Lady Sun; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dazhong, Zhizhong, and Yangzhong, and his younger brothers Yongzhong, Shouzhong, and Bingzhong; his wife was Lady Zou. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Mengyue, registered in a civilian household in Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shangqing, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Minshi, his grandfather Lian, a tribute scholar, and his father Xiang, a county magistrate; his father’s former wife was Lady Zhou, and his mother was Lady Xiong. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Menglin, Menglong, a student of the Directorate of Education, Mengxiong, and Mengzhang; his wife was Lady Xue. He placed twenty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Jian, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Boshou, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Huang, his father Qiao, and his mother Lady Xie; his mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zai and Heng; his wife was Lady Zhao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Rujue, registered in a military household of Longxiang Guard and a native of Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zixiu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Man, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Weiren [?], formerly a battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; his mother was Lady Su. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Ruchi, Rude, Rushan, a tribute scholar, Rushi, a tribute scholar, Ruxue, Rucheng, and Rujian; his wife was Lady Zhu. He placed 118th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jin Shilong, courtesy name Mengyang, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Kunshan County. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Rong, and his father Pei; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Lu. He placed 104th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yi, courtesy name Bangzhi, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An added-quota student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-three, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Mirui, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his grandfather Tan was a County Magistrate, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Administrative Service and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His father was Yunteng, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. He had an elder brother, Yu, and younger brothers Fang, Zhao, Mou, Xun, and Shen. He married a woman née Wu. He placed 27th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Dakun, courtesy name Shihua, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yongying, his grandfather Rui, and his father Liang; his mother was née Wu. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Hong. He placed 62nd in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 44th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Wu, courtesy name Wenyang, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An affiliated student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked eighty-third in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Huang, and his father Zhen. His father's former wife was née Zhou, his mother was née Tang, and his stepmother was née Feng. Both parents were living. He had an elder brother, Huai, and younger brothers Jia, Qi, Yi, and You. He married a woman née Chen. He placed 68th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

浦之浩〔貫山東登州衛，軍籍，直隸嘉定縣人，府學生，治詩經，字子化，行四，年三十三，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖安，祖德〔七品散官〕，父鑰〔州判官〕，前母李氏，母許氏。慈侍下，兄之瀾、濬、津，弟之淵、珠、滀、雲、澗、源、洲、淦，娶梁氏，繼娶王氏。山東鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百四十一名。
translation_en:
Lu Jian 陸鑑 was registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziming, and he ranked sixty-third in family order. He was thirty-six years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zonggui; his grandfather, Lu, held an honorary office for longevity; his father was Cai, and his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Teng and Xiang, and his younger brother was Zai. He married a woman née Bao. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Dashao 宋大勺 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daocheng, and he ranked eleventh in family order. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Kai, was a Prefectural School Professor; his grandfather, Xiang, was a Post Station Master; his father was Ren. His mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dashao 大韶, Dazhang, Dawu (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and Dayuan (an official awaiting selection for appointment); his younger brothers were Daqi and Dayuan 大淵. He married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Leng Qiyuan 冷起元 was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. He was a county school student and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jizhen, and he ranked first in family order. He was twenty-three years old, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Duan; his grandfather was Biao; his father, Ang, was a County School Instructor; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiyu and Qizhen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pu Zhihao 浦之浩 was registered in a military household of the Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Jiading County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a prefectural school student and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihua, and he ranked fourth in family order. He was thirty-three years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, De, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father, Yue, was an Assistant Prefect of a subprefecture. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhilan, Jun, and Jin; his younger brothers were Zhiyuan, Zhu, Chu, Yun, Jian, Yuan, Zhou, and Gan. He married a woman née Liang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Ke, registered in Taihu County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zijian. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jiliang, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Yi, an honorary official for longevity; his mother was née Hong. Both parents were living. His younger brother was He, and his wife was née Sun. He ranked eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yangzhi, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and served as Instructor at the county school of Tangxi, Zhejiang. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Junshan. First in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyuan, his grandfather Shining, and his father Congwei; his father's former wife was née Wei, and his mother was née Su. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yangjing, Yangshun, Yangmeng, Deyong, and Deji; his wife was née Huang. He ranked eighty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Da, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shijian. Sixth in birth order, he was aged twenty-three and was born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Suihong, his grandfather Tianjian, and his father Yu, an Instructor at the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan, Xun, Xian, and Zao; his wife was née Huang. He ranked eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei He, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shiyong. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jiyue, his grandfather Chunxing, and his father Shu, an Assistant Prefect; his father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zan, Xian, a Station Master, Gong, a sacrificial official (shengji guan), and Zhi; his wife was née Nie. He ranked thirteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

魏希相〔貫山西太原府陽曲縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字漢卿，行三，年三十三，六月十二日生〕。曾祖欽，祖剛，父通，母張氏。嚴侍下，兄茂、盛，娶李氏，繼娶陳氏。山西鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百三十二名。

張重〔貫順天府昌平州順義縣官籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝任，行三，年三十二，十二月二十五日生〕。曾祖欽〔指揮僉事〕，祖瑀〔指揮僉事〕，父緒〔義官〕，前母趙氏、郭氏，母宋氏。具慶下，兄維藩〔指揮僉事〕、喬〔監生〕，弟香〔陰陽官〕、秉、裏、厚、曆、策，娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第一百二十四名。

李長盛〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學生，治書經，字宗裕，行一，年三十七，八月二十五日生〕。曾祖玘，祖濬〔府通判〕，父孚先〔知州〕，母黃氏，繼母毛氏。具慶下，弟長芳、日新、震、長泰，娶林氏，繼娶楊氏。福建鄉試第三名，會試第二百五十名。
translation_en:
Wen Xian 聞賢, courtesy name Guobin, was registered in an official household of Yongning Guard, Guizhou. An additional student of the guard school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather Zhilian, and his father Yue. His father's former wife was née Zhou, his mother née Qian, and his stepmothers née Zhao, née Zhang, and née Ding. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhi and Shi. He married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed tenth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Xixiang 魏希相, courtesy name Hanqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Gang, his father Tong, and his mother née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Mao and Sheng. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhong 張重, courtesy name Ruren, was registered in an official household in Shunyi County, Changping Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Qin and grandfather Yu were both Assistant Commanders; his father Xu was an Honorary Official. His father's former wives were née Zhao and née Guo, and his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weifan, an Assistant Commander, and Qiao, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Xiang, an official of yin-yang studies, Bing, Li, Hou, Li, and Ce. He married a woman née Guo. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Changsheng 李長盛, courtesy name Zongyu, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather Jun was an Assistant Prefect; and his father Fuxian was a Subprefect. His mother was née Huang and his stepmother née Mao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Changfang, Rixin, Zhen, and Changtai. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

彭謹〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，江西臨江府新淦縣人，山東沂州學正，治春秋，字德全，行六，年三十七，二月初六日生〕。曾祖鈞，祖彥珪，父大綱，母趙氏。永感下，兄誠、謙，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第八十四名，會試第七十九名。

translation_en:
Lin Song 林松, courtesy name Qiaonian, was registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Qian, his father Jiu, and his mother née Xie. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Chun, Huai, Xiang, and Kai, and his younger brother was Bai. He married a woman née Yang. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Paixing 何派行, courtesy name Yingchong, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangshan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Tao, his father Shilong, and his mother née Li. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Paizheng, Paicong, Paixu, and Paixun. He married a woman née Yan. He placed sixteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Jin 彭謹, courtesy name Dequan, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Instructor in Yizhou, Shandong, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Yangui, his father Dagang, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Cheng and Qian. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed eighty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Yu 潘璵, courtesy name Luzhen, was registered in an artisan household in Chengdu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was sixth in birth order, aged forty-eight, and born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzheng; his grandfather Hong held honorary official status for longevity; his father Bojian was an Instructor; and his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Xuan. He married a woman née Ke and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Zixing, registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Binzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Run, his grandfather Lun, his father Zongbao, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zirong and Zihua, and his wife was née Cai. He placed twenty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Cai, registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maozai; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and was twenty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Hua, his father Wenxian, and his mother née Chai. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Cheng, Zhi, Lai, He, and Zhong; his younger brothers were Bing, Rang, Ji, and Nie. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zongqi, registered in an officer household of the Yan'an Guard, Shaanxi, was a native of Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a student of the Yan'an prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zizheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xin was Regional Military Commissioner and was awarded the title General Who Guards the State; his grandfather Cong was a County Vice Magistrate, advanced to the prestige title Gentleman of the Civil Service (wenlin lang). His father was Shiyu, his mother née Chen, and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongyuan, an Imperial University student, Zongyi, and Zongli. His wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yi, registered in a military household in Yuzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruren; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather Qi held an honorary rank for longevity; his father Changlong was a Prefectural Vice Prefect. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Wen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi and Qiao, and his younger brothers Wei and Ren. His wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

金蕃〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字世宣，行十一，年三十，九月初七日生〕。曾祖思仁，祖慎，父鎮，母黃氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，兄葵，弟芥、萊、蒙、蓁，娶宋氏。浙江鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百十六名。

胡彥〔貫湖廣沔陽衛中千戶所官籍，國子生，治書經，字釋美，行二，年四十，十月十一日生〕。曾祖讓，祖鳳臯，父紀〔壽官〕，母宋氏，繼母楊氏。具慶下，兄靖，弟新、韶、端、龍，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第三名，會試第五十三名。
translation_en:
Ruan Wu, courtesy name Dezai, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Xiangfu County, Henan. An additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Tuan, held an honorary title for public benefactions; his father was Shan, and his mother was née Qiang. His father alone was living. His younger brothers were Kun, Bi, and Tang. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zongren, courtesy name Zhongju, was registered in a military household in Wei County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Tong; and his father, Ce. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tan, and he married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Fan, courtesy name Shixuan, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eleventh in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Siren; his grandfather, Shen; and his father, Zhen. His mother was née Huang, and his stepmother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Jie, Lai, Meng, and Zhen. He married a woman née Song. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yan, courtesy name Shimei, was registered in an official household of the Central Battalion of Mianyang Guard, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Fenggao; and his father, Ji, who held an honorary title for longevity. His mother was née Song, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Xin, Shao, Duan, and Long. He married a woman née Liu. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐岱〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，軍籍，府學生，治易經，字太丘，行一，年二十五，六月十一日生〕。曾祖伯順，祖俊，父麒，嫡母傅氏，生母章氏。具慶下，兄山、康，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第二十五名，會試第一百六十四名。

宋治〔貫直隸鳳陽府臨淮縣，軍籍，定遠縣人，直隸內黃縣學教諭，治易經，字時雍，行一，年三十，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖玘，祖祥，父良，前母金氏，母徐氏。慈侍下，弟寧、思、明、清、淳、潔、溥，娶祖氏。順天府鄉試第五十三名，會試第一百六十八名。

王三聘〔貫山東登州府黃縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字伯衡，行一，年三十五，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖成，祖禧〔衛知事〕，父瑤〔監生〕，母郭氏，繼母方氏。具慶下，弟三顧、三讓，娶趙氏。山東鄉試第五名，會試第九十九名。
translation_en:
Wang Jiluo, registered in Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xicheng, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was aged thirty-five [?; the transcription has 生 where 年 is expected], born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Zhi, his father Lian, and his mother née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jilian, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Dai, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Taiqiu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was aged twenty-five, born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Boshun, his grandfather Jun, and his father Qi; his father's principal wife was née Fu, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan and Kang, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Zhi, registered in Linhuai County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was originally from Dingyuan County. He served as Instructor at the county school in Neihuang, Zhili. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiyong, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Liang; his father's former wife was née Jin, and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ning, Si, Ming, Qing, Chun, Jie, and Pu, and his wife was née Zu. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Sanpin, registered in Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Boheng, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather Xi was a Clerk in a guard, and his father Yao was a National University student. His mother was née Guo and his stepmother née Fang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sangu and Sanrang, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

方大樂〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字憲夔，行二，年三十六，十月十四日生〕。曾祖文謨，祖思善〔義官〕，父仲紳，母林氏。嚴侍下，兄大順〔貢士〕，弟大恩、大章、大愷、大本、大觀、大旭。娶林氏，繼娶黃氏。福建鄉試第八十名，會試第八十二名。
translation_en:
Jiang Shan, registered in a military household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shuzhen, he ranked fourteenth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jizu; his grandfather was Yineng, who held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Hong; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xinmin, granted the title of Assistant Judge in the Court of Judicial Review; Fu; Yu [?]; Ying, a Ceremonial Usher; Yi, a Prefect; Meng, an Assistant Judge in the Court of Judicial Review; Chong, granted the honorary cap and girdle; Jian, a Battalion Commander; Ying; and Po, an official awaiting selection for appointment. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yinxian, registered in a military household in Shouzhang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zirong, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-one, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather was Nai, and his father was Jin, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yinfang and Yinxiu. He married a woman née Meng. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in a military household in Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ruming, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Cai, his grandfather was Gui, his father was Tingbin, and his mother was née Xiong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lin and Ting, and his younger brother was Mu. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Dale, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiankui, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenmo; his grandfather was Sishan, who held an honorary title for charitable contributions; his father was Zhongshen; and his mother was née Lin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Dashun, a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Da'en, Dazhang, Dakai, Daben, Daguan, and Daxu. He married a woman née Lin and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed eightieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhu Shunmin, courtesy name Chongyufu, was registered in a civilian household in Qidong County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather, Xuan; and his father, Shixian, a Case Reviewer. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yaomin, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yue, courtesy name Zhunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Bin, held an honorary title for longevity; and his father was Zhang. His mother was née Yao. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Quan, Ke, and Qiao; his younger brother was Tan. His wife was née Hu. He ranked forty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chao Li, courtesy name Junshi, was registered in an artisan household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Wang; and his father, Delong. His father's former wife was née Zhao, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, an Honorary Official; his younger brothers were Pu, a Station Master, and Zhang, Fan, Jin, and Xiu. His wife was née Zhang. He ranked 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Bo, courtesy name Yuefu, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather, Zi, a Chief Officer; and his father, Yu. His mother was née Hu, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Chen, Fen, Fei, Wu, Ke, and Bian. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He ranked eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.
