translation_en:
Cao Tianxian, courtesy name Hengqing, was registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was eighth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangren; his grandfather, Jing, was posthumously or honorifically appointed Magistrate; his father, Tan, was a county school Instructor; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ci, Tianxiang (an Imperial University student), and Tianwen (an Imperial University student); his younger brothers were Tianzhang, Tianfeng, Tianchi, and Tianqiu. His wife was née Cheng. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Zaidao, courtesy name Yiwen, was registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianyou; his grandfather, Yu, was a Registrar in a Guard; his father, Mu, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His wife was née Cheng. He placed ninety-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jin, courtesy name Gonghua, was registered in Mi County, Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ying, was a Medical Instructor; his grandfather, Fu, was a Chief Judicial Officer in a princely establishment; his father, Ding, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shou and Fei. His wife was née Liu, and he subsequently married a woman née Meng. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shan, courtesy name Sijing, was registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Xun; his father was Jingxian; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing and Dao, and his younger brothers were Shi, Shi, and You [? division of the brothers’ names is uncertain]. His wife was née Yu. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shilin, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and originally from Min County, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shangqing, he ranked eighth in his family, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao, his grandfather Cai, and his father Zexing〔an official awaiting selection for appointment〕; his father's former wife was née Qi, and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Shiji, Jin, and Liang, and his younger brothers Shiyong, Yang, Jin, Di, Rui, Zhan, Yao, and Zhang; he married a woman née Lin. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shou, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Renzhong, he ranked second in his family, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin〔honorarily appointed a prefect〕, his grandfather Xiang〔a clerk in the Salt Distribution Commission〕, and his father Gao〔a steward〕; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, Cai, and Guan, and his younger brothers Chong and Chen; he married a woman née Fan. He placed sixty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jizong, registered in a civilian household in Chaocheng County, Pu Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, and originally from Yongfeng County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Kecheng, he ranked second in his family, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiufu, his grandfather Dongrong, and his father Peng; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jixian; he married a woman née Feng. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Guangyu, registered in a military household in Zitong County, Jian Subprefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Siwen, he ranked third in his family, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Wenliang〔an honorary official recognized for longevity〕, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Zhao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Guangzu〔an annual tribute student〕and Guangqi; he married a woman née Shen. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

路伯鏜〔貫南京龍江左衛，官籍，山西陽曲縣人，應天府學附學生，治書經，字元振，行一，年三十六，十月十五日生〕。曾祖順〔副千戶〕，祖暹〔副千戶〕，父通〔副千戶〕，母王氏。慈侍下，弟仲鎧，娶李氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第三十九名。
translation_en:
Chen Yiqin, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked first in birth order, was thirty-one, and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Heng, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Xin, a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Dace, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hongde, Zongde, and Yizhong, and his younger brother was Yilian. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qia, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wende; he ranked third in birth order, was thirty-nine, and was born on the twentieth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yonglong; his grandfather was Qi, a prestige official; his father was Ci, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi and Jia. He married a woman née Niu. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Weizhong, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daoyuan; he ranked third in birth order, was thirty-one, and was born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ruichang; his grandfather was Huan; his father was Ji, granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; and his mother was née Li, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengzhong, Shuzhong, Hengzhong, and Shenzhong, the last a Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His younger brothers were Xingzhong, Jingzhong, Kaizhong, and Zhizhong. He married a woman née Lin. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Botang was registered in an official household of the Longjiang Left Guard in Nanjing and was a native of Yangqu County, Shanxi. He was an additional student at the Yingtian prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanzhen; he ranked first in birth order, was thirty-six, and was born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Shun, grandfather Xian, and father Tong were all Vice Battalion Commanders; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brother was Zhongkai. He married a woman née Li. He placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mei Shoude, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a military household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. Fourth in family order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Kai; his father, Jixian; and his mother, née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shouren, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Shouyue; his younger brothers were Shouxun, Shouzhong, and Shouxin. He married a woman née Guo. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Pei, courtesy name Konglin, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. Seventeenth in family order, he was forty-two years old and was born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather, Bai; his father, Qi; and his mother, née Mao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Ji and Kongming; the latter held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness (yiguan). He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Weicheng, courtesy name Boming, was registered in a military household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. First in family order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shihao; his grandfather, Liangkai; his father, Yue; his mother, née Wang 汪; and his stepmother, also née Wang 汪. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weifan and Weitiao. He married a woman née Wang 汪 and subsequently a woman née Chen. He ranked first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shou, courtesy name Yizhu, was registered in a civilian household in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Second in family order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanguang, a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Jie; his father, Zhizhi; his mother, née Wang 王; and his stepmother, née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ying; his younger brothers were Shen, Bian, Chou, Sao, Zhu, Zhen, Jiao, Zuan, Kai, Bin, Hui, Xuan, and Xu. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Wang 王. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Jiefu, registered in Fucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shijie. His family birth order is garbled as “二三十” [?]. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mingzan; his grandfather, Mao, was a Police Chief; and his father, Shan, was an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lianfu and Qianfu; his younger brothers were Kunfu, Zhongfu, Xiaofu, Zhefu, and Wanfu. His wife was née Liu. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Liang, registered in Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zichong. Second in family birth order, he was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Jing; and his father, Guozheng. His mother was née Shao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Qiao, and his younger brother Zi. His wife was née Bi. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Maohe, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weijie. Third in family birth order, he was twenty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Wengong; and his father, Chao. His mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Jun and Zeng; his younger brothers were Ju, Cheng, Huang, and Shu. His wife was née Hu. He placed seventy-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ji, registered in Ningqiang Guard, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a Hanzhong prefectural-school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Jichuan. First in family birth order, he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Deming, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather, Cong, was a County Registrar; and his father was Yang. His mother was née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gou, Dong, Fei, Qiao, Mei, Huai, Ke, and Nan. His wife was née Ma. He placed forty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

梁紹儒〔貫山東兖州府東平州，民籍，州學生，治易經，字存業，行二，年三十三，六月初四日生〕。曾祖安〔知縣，贈監察御史〕，祖覲〔按察司副使〕，父穀〔吏部主事〕，母孔氏。慈侍下，兄紹先〔監生〕、紹胤〔州學生〕、紹洙，弟紹光〔監生〕、紹元、紹曾、紹奇〔監生〕、紹貞、紹榮、紹寵、紹陽、紹隱、紹策，娶鄭氏。山東鄉試第十一名，會試第二百五十三名。

黃封〔貫四川夔州府雲陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字伯勳，行一，年三十，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖永壽，祖春，父文相，嫡母郭氏，生母趙氏。具慶下，兄流、鶴，弟河、屋、扉、震，娶向氏。四川鄉試第二十五名，會試第二百三十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Yingzhong, registered in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maofu; he ranked eighth in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Zan, his father Mi, and his mother née Chen. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Yingjun; his younger brothers were Yingjing, Yingzeng, Yingxian, and Yingzhao. He married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yingzheng, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhengmeng; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jing'an, his grandfather Xian, his father Yong (County Registrar), and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wu. He placed sixtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Shaoru, registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Cunye; he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was An (District Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor), his grandfather Jin (Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission), his father Gu (Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel), and his mother née Kong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shaoxian (Imperial University student), Shaoyin (subprefectural government school student), and Shaozhu; his younger brothers were Shaoguang (Imperial University student), Shaoyuan, Shaozeng, Shaoqi (Imperial University student), Shaozhen, Shaorong, Shaochong, Shaoyang, Shaoyin, and Shaoce. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Feng, registered in Yunyang County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boxun; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongshou, his grandfather Chun, and his father Wenxiang. His father's principal wife was née Guo, and his birth mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Liu and He; his younger brothers were He, Wu, Fei, and Zhen. He married a woman née Xiang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Denggao, registered in a military household of the Puzhou Battalion, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a native of Hanyang County, Huguang, and a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zisheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Rui, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his father was Shangwen, and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Dengming, Dengxian, Deng’an, and Dengshi, and his wife was née Feng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Weining, registered in a military household of Zhenshuo Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Taiping County, Shanxi, and a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gonghuai; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sirang; his grandfather was Ao; his father was Quan; his father’s former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yong, and his wife was née Wang. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huo Xun, registered in an official household of Yongchang Guard, Yunnan, was a student of the Yongchang Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yunan; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Yuan; his father was Sen, and his mother was née Qiu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Xu, and his younger brothers were Zhao and Wei; his wife was née Bai. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Xin, registered in a civilian household of Zhouzhi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zile; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Bin, an honorary official honored for longevity; his grandfather was Ce, a Study Companion; his father was Yinglin, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers are listed as Pa [?], Zuo, and Ke; his wife was née Deng. He placed thirty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

許嗣宗〔貫福建福州府閩縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字紹德，行二，年四十二，三月二十一日生〕。曾祖景陽〔禮部主事〕，祖坦〔知府加贈中憲大夫〕，父綸〔七品散官〕，前母鄭氏，母林氏。重慶下，兄郊，弟振宗、亢宗、遠宗、儒宗、超宗、翰宗、定宗、追宗、慎宗，娶曾氏。福建鄉試第三十名，會試第二百九十二名。

陳炣〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字文晦，行五，年二十六，八月二十三日生〕。曾祖景蕃，祖邦瑞〔義官〕，父道〔知州〕，母黃氏。具慶下，兄燦、煥、熺、焞〔所吏目〕，娶施氏。江西鄉試第十四名，會試第二百八十名。

張英〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字彥實，行十，年二十七，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖華玉，祖宏志，父儼時，母林氏。慈侍下，兄雲翔、雲衢、雲翼、雲階，弟普，娶洪氏。福建鄉試第六十一名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
Wang Song 王嵩 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weizhong; he ranked fifty-seventh in family order and was aged thirty-six, born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen, his grandfather Shu, and his father Chun, who received the honorary appointment of Case Reviewer in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review. His mother, née Xiong, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiaoling, Court Rectifier in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, and Gao. His wife was née Wang 汪. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Sizong 許嗣宗 was registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shaode; he ranked second in family order and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingyang, a Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Tan, a Prefect additionally granted the posthumous title Grand Master of Palace Counsel; and his father was Lun, holder of a seventh-rank prestige title. His father's former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Jiao; his younger brothers were Zhenzong, Kangzong, Yuanzong, Ruzong, Chaozong, Hanzong, Dingzong, Zhuizong, and Shenzong. His wife was née Zeng. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ke 陳炣 was registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenhui; he ranked fifth in family order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingfan, his grandfather Bangrui, an honorary official for public benefaction, and his father Dao, a Department Magistrate. His mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Can, Huan, Xi, and Tun, the last a Clerk in a suo office [office unspecified]. His wife was née Shi. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ying 張英 was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yanshi; he ranked tenth in family order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huayu, his grandfather Hongzhi, and his father Yanshi 儼時. His mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brothers were Yunxiang, Yunqu, Yunyi, and Yunjie; his younger brother was Pu. His wife was née Hong. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Zide, courtesy name Shenfu, was registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Bogui; his grandfather, Wen; and his father, Jiang. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother née Tian. Both parents were living. His wife was née Geng. He placed twenty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jiuzhang, courtesy name Gongyi, was registered in an artisan household under the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Hengyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Chaode; his grandfather, Tong; and his father, Dan, Deputy Director of the Office of Palace Manufactures. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jiucheng, a tribute scholar; Jiude, an Imperial University student; Jiuze; Jiuchou; Jiuhe; Jiuxu; and Jiulai. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married women née Sun and née Zhang. He placed 129th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Yu, courtesy name Zida, was registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather, Chun, a County Vice Magistrate officially honored for filial piety; and his father, Jue, a County Magistrate. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan; Chong, an annual tribute student; Qian, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Ning; and Shou. His younger brothers were Chen; Cai, a tribute scholar; Huan; and Ji. His wife was née Tian. He placed twentieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ji, courtesy name Ziyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Xu, Chief of Sacrificial Services; and his father, Yao, a Ceremonial Usher. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan, Zhe, Ke, and Zhao; his younger brothers were Pin and Zhi. His wife was née Tian; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Cai 王材, courtesy name Zinan, was from Xincheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather, Da, was an Assistant Instructor; and his father, Lu, was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Bao, and his stepmothers were née Guo and née Zeng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Biao, Xiu, Xi, Nie, Fei, and Jia. His wife was née Niu. He placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Zugeng 袁祖庚, courtesy name Shengzhi, was from Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and registered in a civilian household. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-three, and was born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Huan, and his father Xiao; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhao, and his younger brother was Zushu. His wife was née Wen; he subsequently married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yongjing 李用敬, courtesy name Zhongxue, was from Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Zhan, and his father Jian; his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Yonghe, was Right Assistant Judge in the Court of Judicial Review; his younger brother was Yongzhong. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yangmeng 黃養蒙, courtesy name Cunyi, was from Nan'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and registered in a military household. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather, Deping, was posthumously appointed a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his father, Cheng, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Li, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Yangsu, Yanglian, Yangzhi, Yangdao, and Yangxin. His wife was née Liu; he subsequently married a woman née Lin. He placed eightieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Huan 劉宦, courtesy name Shijin, was registered in an officer household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dehua, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Zhongliang; his father was Tingfu; his father's former wife was née Wei, and his mother was née Kang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, a Company Commander, Run, Qing, and Xiang, and his younger brothers were Shang, Guan, Zong, Cai, and Rong [division of brothers' names uncertain]. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yi 周易, courtesy name Zuyi, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-eight, born on the seventeenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather was Shu; his father was Mian, a prefectural Registrar; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Shi, and his wife was née Tang. He placed forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Wei 鄧巍, courtesy name Weicheng, was registered in a military household in Liuyang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziqi; his grandfather was Zongyu; his father was Feng'ao; and his mother was née Yan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Chaoyang, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Yong, also a student of the Directorate of Education, Jing, and Shu. His wife was née Huang. He placed eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiao 王交, courtesy name Zhengjiu, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked thirty-third in his family and was twenty-eight, born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wu; his grandfather was Chong, a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate; his father was E, a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fang, and his younger brothers were Qi, Yan, and Dan. His wife was née Fei; he subsequently married a woman née Xue. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Dayou, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a salt-producing household under military jurisdiction, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanheng; he ranked eighteenth in the family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan, his grandfather Qian, and his father Tan; his mother was née Huang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Dayi and Dazong, and his younger brothers Daxuan, Dabin, Dayu, and Darong. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Congda, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Lüzhen; he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Qi, and his father Yingchen; his mother was née Cao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Congyuan, and his younger brothers Conggao and Congping. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Hua, registered in a civilian household in Lin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuansu; he ranked fourth in the family and was aged thirty-three, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Cong; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin, Qi, and Shu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Chu, registered in an artisan household attached to the Sichuan Weaving and Dyeing Bureau and a native of Chengdu County, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chuqing; he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Yingzu, and his father Gao; his mother was née Deng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jun. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Zaide, registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weiren; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Wenxin, was a department magistrate; his father was Ji, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zaidao; his younger brothers were Zaishi, Zaiyan and Zaixian (both students of the Directorate of Education), and Zaifan. His wife was née Bian. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Luan, registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and originally from Dayu County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingguo; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twentieth day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather was Tang, his father was Xian, and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were E and Feng. His wife was née Lu. He placed forty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui E, registered in a civilian household in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruzhan; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Li, was a stationmaster, posthumously granted the title of supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; his grandfather, Rui, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father, Hai, was a county magistrate; and his mother was née Hou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chong, a battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, Xun, Yan, and Gang; his younger brothers were Kun and Shan. His wife was née Li. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Yanchen, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and originally from Huichang County, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanzhi; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, was posthumously granted the title of investigating censor and subsequently that of prefect; his grandfather, Da, was a vice administration commissioner of the left in a Provincial Administration Commission, promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master for Palace Service; his father, Jian, was a county magistrate; and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Duanchen and Hanchen. His wife was née Zhang, and his subsequent wife was also née Zhang. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳志〔貫直隸德州衛官籍，直隸宿松縣人，州學生，治禮記，字惟學，行三，年三十五，七月十三日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖祥，父紀，母張氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄忠、懋，娶黃氏。山東鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百八十六名。
translation_en:
Peng Shijue, courtesy name Maoxian, was registered in a military household in Anyue County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Dafu was posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman for Rendering Service and the office of Vice Commander of a Wardens’ Office; his grandfather Lan was an Assistant Prefect. His father was Ji, and his mother was née Dong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shilu, Shichen, Shixun, Shiqing, Shide, and Shiguan. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Wei, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in a military household in Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. An added-quota student in the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fourteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Haoli, his grandfather Zhiwang, his father Guo, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenfang, Wenzhang, and Wensheng. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Luan, courtesy name Yinghe, was registered in a military household in the Lingzhou Defense Battalion, Shaanxi, and was a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather De, and his father Qing. His legal mother was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Yuan. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Feng and his younger brother He. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhi, courtesy name Weixue, was registered in an official household of the Dezhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Susong County in that region. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Ji. His mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhong and Mao. He married a woman née Huang. He ranked sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

喻希立〔貫河南汝寧府光州光山縣民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字惟中，行三，年四十一，四月初九日生〕。曾祖旭，祖明〔歲貢生〕，父端本〔知縣〕，母甘氏，繼母張氏。永感下，兄希宜、希揆，弟希學〔知縣〕、希純〔廩生〕、希大、希益，娶徐氏。河南鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百五十二名。

translation_en:
Zhang Shuli, courtesy name Zimian, was registered in a civilian household in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guang, a county Registrar; his grandfather was Zongzheng; his father was Zhen; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shuyi, Shushe, Shumo, and Shuyou. His wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tingyong, courtesy name Weifan, was registered in a military household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Instructor in Xuzhou, Henan, specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wencheng; his grandfather was Zhengzhong; his father was Zhonghui; and his mother was née Lin. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Weide, Weiye, and Weixue. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Wu. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xili, courtesy name Weizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Guangzhou Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu; his grandfather was Ming, an annual tribute student; and his father was Duanben, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Gan, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiyi and Xikui; his younger brothers were Xixue, a District Magistrate, Xichun, a government-supported student, Xida, and Xiyi. His wife was née Xu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shiyi, courtesy name Wenfan, was registered in a civilian household in Luancheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Xian, a District Magistrate; his father was Zongzhou; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Han. He placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Ai, courtesy name Liangde, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. Fourth in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Qin, held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father, Jin, was a Food Steward. His legal mother was née Shen and his birth mother née Lu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jue, a Department Magistrate, Fu, and Shun; his younger brothers were Shou, Bao, Shu, and Zhi. His wife was née Guo. He placed 119th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Bangyang, courtesy name Sixian, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. Third in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yixun, his grandfather Lu, his father Xiang, and his mother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Bangyan; his younger brothers were Bangzhen, Bangda, and Bangzheng. His wife was née Zou. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Feng, courtesy name Shoudao, was registered in an officer household of the Hangzhou Right Guard in Zhejiang and was originally from Suzhou Department, Zhili. He was an additional student of the Hangzhou prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was twenty-seven years old and was born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ze, was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather, Ye, held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his father was Lian, his mother née Xu, and his stepmother née Li. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brother, Ru, was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his younger brothers were Hua, Ji, Bi, Yi, Jun, Zhong, and Pei. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Duo, courtesy name Shiming, was registered in a banner household of the Nanjing Rear Guard of the Rear Military Commission and was originally from Changshu County, Zhili. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the nineteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Shen, his father Yong, and his mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Gao and his younger brother Kai. His wife was née Qian. He placed fifty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Chi 陳墀 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Xuanfu; he ranked twenty-first in the family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Lei, received the honorary title of Prefectural Vice Prefect and was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left. His grandfather, Tingjing, was a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate and received successive posthumous grants of the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left. His father, Huan, was Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Right. His mother, née Hu, was granted the title of Lady (shuren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Zhang, was a Confucian scholar attached to the Ministry of Rites. His elder paternal cousins were Kai, Da, Jie (an Administration Assistant Commissioner), and Jie [the name is repeated in the transcription; relationship uncertain, ?]. His younger brothers were Hou, Vice Magistrate of Linjiang County; Sheng, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year; Tun, a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate; Shu, a metropolitan graduate attending administrative service [?]; Wan, a student of the Directorate of Education; and Yin, a prefectural school student. He married a woman née Mao. He placed 101st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiaxiao 王嘉孝 was registered in a military household in Jun Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A subprefectural school student, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Tizeng; he ranked first in the family and was aged forty-two, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Xin, held an honorary office conferred for longevity. His grandfather, Zhang, was a Subprefectural Magistrate, and his father, Shiyong, was a County Magistrate. His father's former wife and his mother were both née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Jiajie. He married a woman née Ren and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed seventy-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Mu 梁木 was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked third in the family and was aged twenty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Qi, was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His grandfather, Qian, held an honorary office for public beneficence. His father was Huan, and his mother was née Kang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were 𥞴 [reading uncertain, ?] and Gu; his younger brothers were Yao, Chu, Mi, Ke, Xiu, Shixuan, and Shijin. He married a woman née Guan and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yingxiong 劉應熊 was registered in a military household in Longxi County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student, he specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Tiyang; he ranked second in the family and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng. His grandfather, Zhongwen, was a Guard Command Registrar, and his father, Yue, was a County Magistrate. His mother was née Ma. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yinglin and Yingzhao; his younger brother was Yingguang. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Junmin, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a scholarly household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Mingfu. He ranked first in family order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Yu, his father Chen, and his mother née Ye. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brothers were Qi, Aimin, and Xinmin. He married a woman née Xu. He placed ninety-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jun, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a man of the Wugong Left Guard. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Boying. He ranked first in family order, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuhai, his grandfather Quan, his father Di, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Zuo, and Ji; his younger brothers were Wei, Jie, Shen, Jie (价), and Xiang. He married a woman née Jia and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed one hundred twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Tingxu, registered in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xunfu. He ranked second in family order, was aged forty-one, and was born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Wu, his father Han, and his mother née Ding. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingxiu, a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Tingrui, Tingxiang, Tingmao, and Tingmei. He married a woman née Yang. He placed seventy-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenyu, registered in Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weixue. He ranked forty-third in family order, was aged twenty-two, and was born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lang, his grandfather Defu, an honorary official, his father Ke, and his mother née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Liangkui, a tribute scholar, and Wenzhong; his younger brothers were Wensi, Wennian, Wenyu (文愈), Wenmao, Wenxian, Wenzhi, and Wentai. He married a woman née Ye. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

龔雲從〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字時際，行一，年二十二，九月十六日生〕。曾祖永慶，祖汝安，父體璣，母周氏。嚴侍下，弟雲仍，娶劉氏。福建鄉試第三十二名，會試第五十八名。

戴仁〔貫四川保寧府劔州江油縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字行父，行一，年三十五，二月初七日生〕。曾祖勝剛，祖金，父榮，母羅氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，弟佶、位，娶葉氏。四川鄉試第六十三名，會試第六十四名。

程良〔貫江西饒州府樂平縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字明輔，行二十七，年四十四，七月初四日生〕。曾祖鳳翔，祖文寬，父永亮，前母楊氏，母詹氏。永感下，兄計，弟謹，娶陶氏，繼娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百七十八名。
translation_en:
Sheng Ruqian, from Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Hengfu. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Jian, and his father Yi, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xin, En, Hui, and Zhi, and his younger brother was Ying. His wife was née Wang. He ranked one hundredth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Yuncong, from Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a military household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shiji. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-two and was born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yongqing, his grandfather Ru'an, and his father Tiji; his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Yunreng, and his wife was née Liu. He ranked thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Ren, from Jiangyou County, Jian Subprefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xingfu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shenggang, his grandfather Jin, and his father Rong; his mother was née Luo and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji and Wei, and his wife was née Ye. He ranked sixty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Liang, from Leping County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Mingfu. Twenty-seventh in birth order, he was aged forty-four and was born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Fengxiang, his grandfather Wenkuan, and his father Yongliang; his father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Zhan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ji and his younger brother Jin. His wife was née Tao, and he subsequently married a woman née Xiao. He ranked thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡慥〔貫河南南陽府南陽縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字敬夫，行一，年四十，十一月初七日生〕。曾祖昂〔壽官〕，祖瀛，父朝獻，母徐氏。慈侍下，弟恪，娶楊氏。河南鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百八十六名。

劉元凱〔貫四川保寧府閬中縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字舜舉，行一，年二十九，正月十七日生〕。曾祖蕙〔義官〕，祖湖〔義官〕，父光啓〔引禮舍人〕，母白氏。慈侍下，弟元正、元亨，娶李氏。四川鄉試第三名，會試第四十七名。

徐紳〔貫直隸池州府建德縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字思行，行六，年二十六，正月初三日生〕。曾祖公振，祖永清〔義官〕，父黻〔散官〕，前母周氏、楊氏，母汪氏。具慶下，兄輅、驂、曜〔監生〕、翼〔醫學正術〕、縉〔省祭官〕，娶李氏。應天府鄉試第一百八名，會試第五十六名。

吳禎〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字元吉，行一，年三十五，四月十二日生〕。曾祖稷，祖玉〔監生〕，父恩〔陰陽訓術〕，母殷氏，繼母沈氏。慈侍下，弟視、禘、祺〔監生〕、祐、禴，娶莫氏，繼娶虞氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十五名，會試第二百二十四名。
translation_en:
Hu Zao, registered in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ang, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Ying; his father was Chaoxian; and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Ke, and his wife was née Yang. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yuankai, registered in Langzhong County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunju; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Hui and grandfather Hu both held honorary official titles for public benefactions; his father, Guangqi, was a Court Usher; and his mother was née Bai. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yuanzheng and Yuanheng, and his wife was née Li. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Shen, registered in Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Sixing; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongzhen; his grandfather, Yongqing, held an honorary official title for public benefactions; and his father, Fu, held prestige rank without a substantive appointment. His father's former wives were née Zhou and née Yang, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu, Can, Yao, an Imperial University student, Yi, a Medical Officer, and Jin, a Sacrificial Attendant. His wife was née Li. He placed 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhen, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanji; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Yu, was an Imperial University student; his father, En, was an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; his mother was née Yin; and his stepmother was née Shen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shi, Di, Qi, an Imperial University student, You, and Yue. His wife was née Mo, and he subsequently married a woman née Yu. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

宋岳〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣竈籍，府學生，治易經，字伯鎮，行一，年二十六，十二月二十八日生〕。曾祖璿〔封刑部主事，贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖冕〔通議大夫，都察院右副都御史〕，父惟明〔官生〕，母姜氏。重慶下，弟巒、山、岠、崧、嵓，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第六十四名，會試第六十名。
translation_en:
Hua Yun, courtesy name Conglong, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged fifty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bensheng; his grandfather was Dong; his father was Linxiang, Chief Clerk in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Dian, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Lu. He married a woman née Yang. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tinggao, courtesy name Shuqian, was registered in a civilian household in Jinxiang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Chongren County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Chun, a County Registrar; his grandfather was Jin; and his father was Kui, an Assistant Instructor. His legal mother was née Tang, and his birth mother was née Lü. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingxiu, Tingcui, and Tingmao. He married a woman née Zu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yueran, courtesy name Rucong, was registered in a military household attached to the Weihui Guarding Battalion in Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Su, an Assistant Prefect; his grandfather was Qing, an Imperial University student; his father was Shi'en; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yueke and Yueshan. He married a woman née Cao. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yue, courtesy name Bozhen, was registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and posthumously awarded that of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather was Mian, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Weiming, a student admitted by virtue of an official's privilege, and his mother was née Jiang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Luan, Shan, Ju, Song, and Yan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

周奎〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字賢象，行四，年二十八，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖秉章，祖古憲，父望前，母郭氏、蔡氏，母郭氏。具慶下，兄黃、持、體，弟斛、虛、房、蟾、棟、華、井，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Sun Wei 孫渭, courtesy name Yingqing, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zifen; his grandfather, Tang; and his father, Tong. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ye, and his younger brother was Ze. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui Ren 貴仁, courtesy name Ziren, was registered with the Imperial Medical Institute and was a native of Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Mao, was an Imperial Physician; his grandfather, Xuan, was a Medical Director; and his father was Sheng. His mother was née Zong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Ru, Yu, Shi, Shen, Lun, Feng, and Xiang. His wife was née Weng. He placed third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Yunyue 應雲鸑, courtesy name Ruibo, was registered in a military household in Xiangshan County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jie, was an Instructor; his grandfather, Yuanzheng, was a Vice Prefect; and his father was Zhensu. His mother was née Xie. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Yunlong; his younger brothers were Yunhuang, Yunzhuo, Yunpeng, Yunhan, Yunkun, and Yunqian. His wife was née Bao, and his subsequent wife was also née Bao. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Kui 周奎, courtesy name Xianxiang, was registered in a civilian household in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingzhang; his grandfather, Guxian; and his father, Wangqian. The text lists his mothers as née Guo and née Cai, then repeats “mother née Guo” [?]. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huang, Chi, and Ti; his younger brothers were Hu, Xu, Fang, Chan, Dong, Hua, and Jing. His wife was née Xiao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

梁成〔貫山東兗州府平陰縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字公濟，行三，年三十，六月二十三日生〕。曾祖英，祖俊〔府照磨〕，父棟〔縣丞〕，母趙氏。慈侍下，兄金、善，娶尹氏。山東鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百九十六名。
translation_en:
Zhang Xi 張習, courtesy name Zichong, was registered in a civilian household in Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Yan; and his father, Li, who received the honorary titles Gentleman for Attendant Service and Secretariat Drafter. His mother, née Chen, received the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lan, Hui, Zhi, Kui, and Yi; his younger brothers were Dan, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Zai, Fan, Zao, Mao, and Yin. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Jiguang 潘繼光, courtesy name Maoxue, was registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Quan; his father, Xiong; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jizong. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fengkai 劉逢愷, courtesy name Yurang, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was tenth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shisheng; his grandfather, Wang; his father, Duanxiang; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fengyuan, Fengji, Fengnian, Fengchun, Fenggen, Fengtang, Fengwen, Fengtai, and Fengshu; his younger brothers were Fengzhi and Fengxiao. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He ranked fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Cheng 梁成, courtesy name Gongji, was registered in a civilian household in Pingyin County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Jun, a prefectural Records Examiner; his father, Dong, a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother, née Zhao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jin and Shan. He married a woman née Yin. He ranked forty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Mian, registered in a military household in Xiaofeng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Fuzhou; he ranked fourth in the family and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Guan, his father Kui, and his mother née Mei. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Sheng, Tan, and Xing; his wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Bi, registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaowan; he ranked second in the family and was aged forty, born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Chun was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works. His grandfather Gao was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel. His father was Hui, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhu, and his younger brothers were Chen, Guan, Pu, Zao, Xi, and Lang; his wife was née Ji. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Pei, registered in a civilian household in Dezhou, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Fuyu; he ranked second in the family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather Zhen, his father Long, an honorary official (yiguan), and his mother née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Lian, Gong, and Xuan; his wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yu, registered in a civilian household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was Instructor at the Huichang County Confucian School in Jiangxi and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruliang; he ranked first in the family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Zhe, his father Dezong, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, Sui, and Xuan; his wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
于德昌〔貫四川成都左護衛軍籍，華陽縣人，國子生，治書經，字子順，行三，年三十六，四月十二日生〕。曾祖師鑑，祖顯，父輝祖〔府同知，進階朝列大夫〕，母羅氏。嚴侍下，兄德興、德裔，弟德佑〔貢士〕、德宜。娶王氏，繼娶潘氏。四川鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百九十八名。

朱應奎〔貫錦衣衛匠籍，直隸丹陽縣人，國子生，治易經，字士徴，行一，年三十八，六月十五日生〕。曾祖福海，祖玉，父文，嫡母毛氏，生母徐氏。慈侍下，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百七十六名。

谷鍾秀〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字毓卿，行二，年三十七，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖志，祖應，父明，母王氏。永感下，兄鍾靈，弟鍾祥、鍾清、鍾和、鍾華、鍾美、鍾良、鍾粹、鍾醇、鍾淑、鍾正、鍾一。娶張氏。浙江鄉試第十五名，會試第三十五名。

趙珆〔貫四川叙州府富順縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字子獻，行三，年三十六，七月二十五日生〕。曾祖學，祖伯香，父承準〔官壽〕，母先氏，繼母丘氏。具慶下，兄珂、璟。娶劉氏。四川鄉試第五十名，會試第一百三十八名。
translation_en:
Yu Dechang, courtesy name Zishun, was registered in a military household of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard in Sichuan and was a native of Huayang County. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shijian; his grandfather, Xian; and his father, Huizu, a prefectural vice prefect promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master of Court Rank. His mother was née Luo. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Dexing and Deyi; his younger brothers were Deyou, a tribute scholar, and Deyi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Pan. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Yingkui, courtesy name Shizheng, was registered in an artisan household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Danyang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Fuhai; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Wen. His legal mother was née Mao, and his birth mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Zhongxiu, courtesy name Yuqing, was registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Ming; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zhongling; his younger brothers were Zhongxiang, Zhongqing, Zhonghe, Zhonghua, Zhongmei, Zhongliang, Zhongcui, Zhongchun, Zhongshu, Zhongzheng, and Zhongyi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yi 趙珆, courtesy name Zixian, was registered in a civilian household of Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xue; his grandfather, Boxiang; and his father, Chengzhun, whose annotation reads “official; longevity” [?]. His mother was née Xian, and his stepmother was née Qiu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ke and Jing. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fiftieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.
