十有四曰祭天地社稷也山川城隍也日月
風雲雷雨也嶽鎮海瀆也先聖先師祀典神
祇也嘉禮五曰朝會朋拜也曰冠昏鄉飲也
賓禮二曰朝貢也遣使也軍禮三曰親征也
punctuated:
陽脩曰：「三代而下，治出于二，而禮樂徒為虛文。」此也。盖禮樂者，為治之道也，而六經所陳，亦不能外此以為之用。如書之命夷命夔，易之定志殷薦，春秋之兩觀六羽，何者而不相通于道耶？然則漢史所謂「六經之道同歸，而禮樂之用為急」者，義固有所偏也。禮樂者，為治之本也，而政刑所在，亦惟輔其治之所不及。如唐虞士師之官，商人官刑之儆，成周司寇之屬，是豈盛世之所偏廢哉？然則聖制所謂「政刑末務，果不足以為治」者，意固有所所在也。
洪惟太祖高皇帝，獨稟全智，超越千古，明華夏于既污，復衣冠于左衽。乃于開天肇紀之初，即以禮樂為急，徵賢分局，講究切劘。爰命牛諒制禮，而大禮以定。其載諸集禮者，則吉禮十有四，曰祭天地社稷也，山川城隍也，日月風雲雷雨也，嶽鎮海瀆也，先聖先師祀典神祇也；嘉禮五，曰朝會冊拜也，曰冠昏鄉飲也；賓禮二，曰朝貢也，遣使也；軍禮三，曰親征也。
translation_en:
…Ouyang Xiu said: “After the Three Dynasties, government proceeded from two separate sources, and rites and music became mere empty forms.” This is what he meant. Rites and music are the Way of governing, and what the Six Classics set forth likewise cannot operate outside them. Consider the appointments of Yi and Kui in the Book of Documents, the settling of intentions and the sumptuous offerings in the Book of Changes, and the two gate towers and six ranks of feather-bearing dancers in the Spring and Autumn Annals: which of these does not communicate with the others through the Way? Thus the statement in the History of the Han that “the Ways of the Six Classics converge upon the same end, but the application of rites and music is most urgent” is certainly partial in its meaning. Rites and music are the foundation of government, while administration and punishments merely supplement those areas their governance does not reach. Consider the office of Judge under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, the Shang people’s admonitions concerning punishments for officials, and the personnel under the Minister of Justice of the Zhou: could these have been neglected in an age of flourishing rule? Thus Your Majesty’s statement, “Administration and punishments are secondary concerns; are they indeed insufficient for governing?” surely has a particular intent [the transcription repeats a character here].
Reverently considering Emperor Taizu Gao, he alone was endowed with consummate wisdom, surpassing all preceding ages. He restored the glory of Chinese civilization after its defilement and restored Chinese caps and robes in place of garments fastened on the left. At the very beginning of his founding of the dynasty, he therefore made rites and music an urgent priority, summoning worthy men and assigning them to separate bureaus to investigate, discuss, and refine them. He then commanded Niu Liang to establish the rites, and the great rites were thereby settled. As recorded in the Collected Rites, there were fourteen auspicious rites: sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the altars of Soil and Grain; to mountains and rivers and city gods; to the sun and moon, wind, clouds, thunder, and rain; to the sacred peaks, guardian mountains, seas, and great waterways; and to former sages, former teachers, and the spirits included in the sacrificial canon. There were five celebratory rites: court assemblies and investitures, capping ceremonies, marriages, and village drinking ceremonies. There were two guest rites: the presentation of tribute at court and the dispatch of envoys. There were three military rites: the emperor’s taking the field in person…

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
遣將大將也凶禮二曰弔賻喪儀也他如冠
服車輅儀仗鹵簿莫不秩有定制順于鬼神
合于人心至精而至密所以教天下之敬者
何至也又
命陶凱制樂而大樂以成其載諸集禮者則有曰
本太初曰仰大明曰民初生曰品物亨曰御
六龍曰泰階平曰君德成曰聖道成曰樂清
寧他如黃鐘大呂管籥干羽莫不雅有定式
以和神人以諧上下盡善而盡美所以宣天
下之和者何至也是以禮讓之美達于黎庶
===
絃歌之聲徹于閭閻而禮樂教化信乎蔚然
于安居樂業之中矣但
聖人有作固皆出于不思不勉之德而
天造草昧或猶歉于可久可大之規是以道不虛
行而事必有待也肆我
皇上纘承大統
仁孝之德本乎天縱
聖敬之學由于日躋
踐祚以來不遑他務首以人倫典禮是圖是故
明大倫之典則父子之位定而繼統繼嗣之義昭

明大倫之典則父子之位定而繼統繼嗣之義昭
punctuated:
遣將、大將也。凶禮二，曰弔賻、喪儀也。他如冠服、車輅、儀仗、鹵簿，莫不秩有定制，順于鬼神，合于人心，至精而至密，所以教天下之敬者何至也！又命陶凱制樂，而大樂以成。其載諸《集禮》者，則有曰《本太初》，曰《仰大明》，曰《民初生》，曰《品物亨》，曰《御六龍》，曰《泰階平》，曰《君德成》，曰《聖道成》，曰《樂清寧》。他如黃鐘大呂、管籥干羽，莫不雅有定式，以和神人，以諧上下，盡善而盡美，所以宣天下之和者何至也！是以禮讓之美達于黎庶，絃歌之聲徹于閭閻，而禮樂教化信乎蔚然于安居樂業之中矣。
但聖人有作，固皆出于不思不勉之德，而天造草昧，或猶歉于可久可大之規。是以道不虛行，而事必有待也。肆我皇上纘承大統，仁孝之德本乎天縱，聖敬之學由于日躋。踐祚以來，不遑他務，首以人倫典禮是圖。是故明大倫之典，則父子之位定，而繼統繼嗣之義昭
translation_en:
…dispatching generals, and “great generals” [?]. The two mourning rites are condolence offerings and funeral ceremonies. Other matters, such as caps and robes, ceremonial carriages, ceremonial guards, and processional escorts, all had their established regulations, properly ordered. These accorded with the spirits and satisfied human hearts, being supremely refined and meticulous. How consummate were the means by which reverence was taught throughout the realm!
He also commanded Tao Kai to establish the music, and thus the great ceremonial music was completed. The pieces recorded in the Collected Rituals (Jili) include “Rooted in the Primordial Beginning,” “Looking Up to the Great Luminary,” “When the People First Came into Being,” “The Myriad Things Flourish,” “Driving the Six Dragons,” “The Three Steps Are at Peace,” “The Ruler’s Virtue Is Perfected,” “The Sage’s Way Is Perfected,” and “Rejoicing in Clarity and Tranquillity.” Other elements, such as the Huangzhong and Dalü pitch standards, pipes and flutes, and the shields and feathers used in ritual dances, all had their established, elegant forms. They brought spirits and humans into harmony and concord to those above and below, attaining perfect goodness and beauty. How consummate were the means by which harmony was spread throughout the realm! Thus the beauty of ritual propriety and deference reached the common people, and the sound of strings and singing resounded through the lanes. The transforming influence of rites and music indeed flourished among people dwelling in peace and taking pleasure in their occupations.
Yet although all that a sage institutes proceeds from virtue exercised without deliberation or effort, in the obscure and unsettled beginnings of a new order, the arrangements may still fall short of what can endure and become great. Thus the Way does not put itself into practice unaided, and affairs must await their fulfillment. Now Our Emperor has succeeded to the great imperial line. His benevolence and filial devotion are endowed by Heaven, and his learning in sagely reverence advances daily. Since ascending the throne, he has had no leisure for other business, giving first attention to the canonical rites governing human relationships. Thus, by clarifying the institutions governing the great human relationships, he has fixed the respective positions of father and son and made manifest the distinction between succession to the imperial line and succession as an heir…

translation_en:
…the kinship deriving from a single root is a bond of natural affection that cannot be severed. By elucidating the rites of separate sacrifices, the distinction between Heaven and Earth has been made strict, and the positions of the Circular Mound and the Square Marsh altars established. At the two solstices, yin and yang each receive their due observance in their proper season.
According to the Royal Regulations, the Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples; under the Zhou, permanent temples for Kings Wen and Wu were first established. In establishing its Imperial Ancestral Temple, our dynasty formerly followed the system of separate chambers within a common hall. Now Taizu is honored in the south-facing position and receives offerings alone in a separate temple, honoring him as the founding ancestor for his achievement in establishing the state and laying its foundations. Taizong has been exalted as Chengzu, whose spirit tablet shall never be removed, honoring him as an ancestral sovereign for his virtue in succeeding to the throne and preserving established institutions. The remaining ancestors, arranged in the zhao and mu generations, each have a separate temple; when their kinship falls beyond the prescribed limit, their temples are successively dismantled. How fitting are these measures for establishing the regulations governing ancestral temples!
According to the Royal Regulations, the Son of Heaven performs the spring yue sacrifice separately, and the summer di, autumn chang, and winter zheng sacrifices as joint offerings; every third year there is the rite of the great joint sacrifice. Our dynasty formerly conducted sacrifices at its ancestral temples separately in winter and summer. Now separate offerings are made in the first month of spring to manifest the enduring honor accorded to all the temples. Joint sacrifices are held in the other three seasons to trace the lineage back to its original source. The seasonal sacrifice at the year's end continues to be held at…

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
奉先殿行之所以隆祀事之典何如也
大禘之禮闕而不行者非一日矣今追祀
德祖之所自出而以
太祖配之虛位之設真足以洗世系之誣而如在
之誠感通之妙即禮不王不禘之義也
明堂之制廢而不講者亦有年矣今大享
上帝于
玄極殿而以
睿宗配之季秋之月固有以報成事之休而萬物
本乎天人本乎祖即周人宗祀文王于明堂
===
以配上帝之義也凡若此者奉
天道以周旋本人情而因革以昭百世不刊之典
以破千古不决之疑以立百王不易之法真
足以比隆唐虞三代而仰成我
皇祖未成之典所謂善繼其志而善述其事者也
若猶未也他如肇
親蠶之典以開民衣食之原隆
先師之號以去彼衮冕之侈與夫
大狩有錄冠服有圖何莫而非禮之散見也禮之
所至則樂亦至焉矣

punctuated:
奉先殿行之，所以隆祀事之典何如也？
大禘之禮闕而不行者非一日矣。今追祀德祖之所自出，而以太祖配之，虛位之設，真足以洗世系之誣；而如在之誠、感通之妙，即禮不王不禘之義也。
明堂之制廢而不講者亦有年矣。今大享上帝于玄極殿，而以睿宗配之。季秋之月，固有以報成事之休；而萬物本乎天，人本乎祖，即周人宗祀文王于明堂以配上帝之義也。凡若此者，奉天道以周旋，本人情而因革，以昭百世不刊之典，以破千古不决之疑，以立百王不易之法，真足以比隆唐虞三代，而仰成我皇祖未成之典，所謂善繼其志而善述其事者也。
若猶未也，他如肇親蠶之典，以開民衣食之原；隆先師之號，以去彼衮冕之侈；與夫大狩有錄，冠服有圖，何莫而非禮之散見也？禮之所至，則樂亦至焉矣。
translation_en:
…performed in Fengxian Hall: how do these provisions serve to exalt the sacrificial observances?
The rite of the great di sacrifice has long been left unperformed. Now sacrifice is offered retrospectively to the ancestor from whom Dezu descended, with Taizu associated in the offering. Establishing an unoccupied spirit seat is indeed sufficient to dispel false claims about the lineage. The sincerity of serving the spirits as though present, and the wondrous efficacy of communicating with them, embody the ritual principle that only a king may perform the di sacrifice.
The institution of the Hall of Light has likewise long fallen into disuse and ceased to receive attention. Now the great sacrifice to the Lord on High is offered in Xuanji Hall, with Ruizong associated in the offering. Its performance in the last month of autumn duly expresses gratitude for the blessing of completed labors. All things have their origin in Heaven, and human beings in their ancestors: this embodies the same principle as the Zhou people's ancestral sacrifice to King Wen in the Hall of Light, associating him with the Lord on High. All such measures accord with the Way of Heaven in their conduct and take human feelings as the basis for retaining or changing established practices. They make manifest institutions that cannot be effaced for a hundred generations, resolve doubts left unsettled for a thousand ages, and establish rules that a hundred kings cannot alter. They truly rival the splendor of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and reverently bring to completion the institutions that Our Imperial Ancestor left unfinished. This is what is meant by skillfully carrying on his intentions and continuing his undertakings.
As though these were still insufficient, there are also such measures as inaugurating the rite of personal sericulture to develop the source of the people's clothing and sustenance; exalting the title of the First Teacher, thereby removing the extravagance of his ceremonial robes and crown; and providing records of the great imperial hunts and illustrations of caps and robes. Which of these is not a manifestation of ritual in its various particulars? Wherever ritual reaches, music reaches also.

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
春遊有詠以紀
君臣之同遊欽
天有頌以儼
上帝之臨女與夫除夕之作平臺之詩何莫而非
樂之敷陳也樂之所極則禮亦極焉矣然則
歷代之禮樂固未有如我
朝之盛而我
朝之禮樂亦未有如
今日之尤盛者也則夫仁讓之風淪肌而浹髓
中和之效際天而蟠地豈非勢之所必至哉
而
陛下則慮夫教化未盡孚風俗未盡美災害未盡
殄生養未盡遂是誠治已至而猶以為未至
民已安而猶以為未安也臣則以為禮樂也
者所以同民心而出治道者也所以位天地
而育萬物者也禮樂行則化孚俗美政治民
安固其所也而或有不然者是非可以徒歸
咎諸禮樂也意者為治之道固自有出於禮
樂之外者矣何也致格天之功者固難而尤
難於有憲天之道盡憲天之道者固難而尤

而

殄生養未盡遂是誠治已至而猶以爲未至
民已安而猶以爲未安也臣則以爲禮樂也
者所以同民心而出治道者也所以位天地
而育萬物者也禮樂行則化乎俗美政治民
安固其所也而或有不然者是非可以徒歸
咎諸禮樂也意者爲治之道固自有出於禮
樂之外者矣何也致格天之功者固難而尤
難於有憲天之道盡憲天之道者固難而尤
punctuated:
春遊有詠，以紀君臣之同遊；欽天有頌，以儼上帝之臨女。與夫除夕之作、平臺之詩，何莫而非樂之敷陳也？樂之所極，則禮亦極焉矣。然則歷代之禮樂，固未有如我朝之盛；而我朝之禮樂，亦未有如今日之尤盛者也。則夫仁讓之風，淪肌而浹髓；中和之效，際天而蟠地，豈非勢之所必至哉？
而陛下則慮夫教化未盡孚，風俗未盡美，災害未盡殄，生養未盡遂。是誠治已至而猶以為未至，民已安而猶以為未安也。臣則以為禮樂也者，所以同民心而出治道者也，所以位天地而育萬物者也。禮樂行，則化孚俗美，政治民安，固其所也。而或有不然者，是非可以徒歸咎諸禮樂也。意者為治之道，固自有出於禮樂之外者矣。何也？致格天之功者固難，而尤難於有憲天之道；盡憲天之道者固難，而尤
translation_en:
There are verses on the spring excursion to commemorate the ruler and his ministers journeying together, and a hymn on revering Heaven to inspire reverence for the Lord on High watching over you. Together with the composition for New Year’s Eve and the poem on the Terrace, are these not all expressions of music? Where music reaches its fullest realization, ritual likewise reaches its fullest realization. Thus, the ritual and music of successive dynasties have never flourished as they do under our dynasty; and even within our dynasty, they have never flourished so greatly as today. Must not the spirit of benevolence and deference therefore penetrate flesh and marrow, and the effects of equilibrium and harmony extend to the heavens and encompass the earth?
Yet Your Majesty worries that moral instruction has not fully won the people’s trust, that customs are not wholly good, that disasters have not been entirely eliminated, and that the people’s livelihood and nurture have not been fully secured. Truly, good government has already been achieved, yet you regard it as still unachieved; the people are already at peace, yet you regard them as not yet at peace. Your servant believes that ritual and music are the means of uniting the people’s hearts and bringing forth the Way of governance, of setting Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing the myriad things. When ritual and music are practiced, moral instruction wins trust, customs become good, government is orderly, and the people are at peace: these are their natural results. If things sometimes turn out otherwise, the blame cannot simply be laid upon ritual and music. Perhaps the Way of governance indeed includes something beyond ritual and music. Why is this? Achieving the efficacy that moves Heaven is certainly difficult, but possessing the Way of emulating Heaven is harder still; fully realizing the Way of emulating Heaven is certainly difficult, but even more…

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
莫難於有純天之心蓋非制禮作樂固不足
以為憲天而非建中和之極者亦未可輕以
語夫純天也心者中和之極也中和也者無
體之禮無聲之樂也至禮不讓而天下治矣
至樂無聲而天下和矣此唐虞三代所以為
治之極也今
陛下以純天之心盡憲天之道方且以未臻格天
之功為憂故於
聖制之末復進臣等于有言以為何脩而可以比
隆于先王之盛則臣愚以為天下之治常患
===
乎君臣相遇之難故有是君而不得名世之
佐則輔之者無其人有是臣而不遇王者之
興則主之者無其人是以漢之賈誼有志于
禮樂而文帝謙讓未遑唐之太宗嘗詢乎禮
儀而房杜噤不能對良可慨也今幸遇
聖天子在上賢公卿在下
君臣相遇于斯為盛此正王者必世后仁禮樂百
年可興之期也臣敢不罄言以為
聖化萬分之一助乎蓋人君之所貴者莫貴乎以
禮樂為實用也人君之所病者莫病乎以禮

君臣相遇于斯為盛此正王者必世后仁禮樂百

聖化萬分之一助乎蓋人君之所貴者莫貴乎以

punctuated:
莫難於有純天之心。蓋非制禮作樂，固不足以為憲天；而非建中和之極者，亦未可輕以語夫純天也。心者，中和之極也。中和也者，無體之禮、無聲之樂也。至禮不讓而天下治矣，至樂無聲而天下和矣。此唐虞三代所以為治之極也。今陛下以純天之心，盡憲天之道，方且以未臻格天之功為憂，故於聖制之末，復進臣等于有言，以為何脩而可以比隆于先王之盛？則臣愚以為天下之治，常患乎君臣相遇之難。
故有是君而不得名世之佐，則輔之者無其人；有是臣而不遇王者之興，則主之者無其人。是以漢之賈誼有志于禮樂，而文帝謙讓未遑；唐之太宗嘗詢乎禮儀，而房杜噤不能對。良可慨也！今幸遇聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，君臣相遇，于斯為盛。此正王者必世后仁、禮樂百年可興之期也。臣敢不罄言，以為聖化萬分之一助乎？
蓋人君之所貴者，莫貴乎以禮樂為實用也；人君之所病者，莫病乎以禮
translation_en:
…nothing is more difficult than possessing a heart wholly at one with Heaven. Without instituting rites and creating music, one certainly cannot take Heaven as one’s model; yet unless one establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony, one cannot lightly speak of being wholly at one with Heaven. The heart is the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. Equilibrium and harmony are rites without bodily form and music without sound. Through the highest rites, the world is ordered without ceremonial yielding; through the highest music, the world is harmonious without sound. This is why the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties attained the pinnacle of government. Now Your Majesty, with a heart wholly at one with Heaven, fully realizes the way of taking Heaven as your model, yet remains concerned that you have not achieved the result of moving Heaven. Thus, at the end of your imperial decree, you again invite us, your servants, to offer our views, asking what must be cultivated to equal the flourishing greatness of the former kings. In my humble opinion, the ordering of the world is constantly beset by the difficulty of bringing the right ruler and ministers together.
For when there is such a ruler, but he cannot obtain an assistant renowned in his age, there is no suitable person to aid him; when there is such a minister, but he does not encounter the rise of a true king, there is no suitable person to be his sovereign. Thus Jia Yi of the Han aspired to establish rites and music, but Emperor Wen modestly deferred the undertaking and found no opportunity for it. Emperor Taizong of the Tang once inquired about ritual observances, but Fang and Du remained silent, unable to reply. This is truly lamentable! Now, fortunately, we live under a sagely Son of Heaven, with worthy dukes and high ministers serving below. The coming together of ruler and ministers has reached its height at this moment. This is precisely the occasion envisaged in the sayings that, under a true king, a generation must pass before benevolent rule prevails, and that rites and music can flourish after a hundred years. Dare I fail to speak to the fullest, to contribute even one ten-thousandth part toward Your Majesty’s transforming influence?
For a ruler, nothing is more precious than putting rites and music to practical use; nothing is more harmful than treating rites …

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
樂爲虛文也何為實用本諸心以形諸其身
始于宫闈以達諸朝廷由乎畿甸以風乎天
下者也何謂虛文煩于治臣下而簡于人主
之一身徧于四境而不及乎其家鋪張乎粉
飾太平之具而闊畧于禮讓爲國之實者也
故曰簠簋俎豆制度文章禮之器也升降上
下周旋裼襲禮之文也鐘鼓管磬羽籥干戚
樂之器也屈伸俯仰綴兆疾徐樂之文也又
曰中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之則也
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也蓋
===
禮樂之實不外乎中和之極中和之極不外
乎性情之德而性情之德不外乎主靜慎獨
之功故深宫大庭俱爲一體旦晝夜氣初無
二機誠能自戒懼而約之以至于至靜之地
無少偏倚而其守不失則爲有以致其中矣
自謹獨而精之以至于應物之處無少差謬
而無適不然則爲有以致其和矣乃若土木
之事神仙之技甲兵之釁必絕而去之懼其
有以戾吾之中也世俗之樂鄭衛之音萋菲
之言必放而遠之懼其有以乖吾之和也由

始于宮闈以達諸朝廷由乎畿甸以風乎天

曰中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之則也
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也盖
===
禮樂之實不外乎中和中和之極不外
乎性情之德而性情之德不外乎主靜愼獨
之功故深宮大庭倶爲一體旦晝夜氣初無
二機誠能自戒懼而約之以至于至靜之地
無少偏倚而其守不失則爲有以致其中矣
自謹獨而精之以至于應物之處無少差謬
而無適不然則爲有以致其和矣乃若土木
之事神仙之技甲兵之釁必絶而去之懼其
有以戾吾之中也世俗之樂鄭衛之音妻菲
之言必放而遠之懼其有以乖吾之和也由
punctuated:
樂爲虛文也。何為實用？本諸心以形諸其身，始于宫闈以達諸朝廷，由乎畿甸以風乎天下者也。何謂虛文？煩于治臣下而簡于人主之一身，徧于四境而不及乎其家，鋪張乎粉飾太平之具而闊畧于禮讓爲國之實者也。
故曰：「簠簋俎豆，制度文章，禮之器也；升降上下，周旋裼襲，禮之文也；鐘鼓管磬，羽籥干戚，樂之器也；屈伸俯仰，綴兆疾徐，樂之文也。」又曰：「中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之則也；論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。」
蓋禮樂之實，不外乎中和之極；中和之極，不外乎性情之德；而性情之德，不外乎主靜慎獨之功。故深宫大庭，俱爲一體；旦晝夜氣，初無二機。誠能自戒懼而約之，以至于至靜之地，無少偏倚，而其守不失，則爲有以致其中矣。自謹獨而精之，以至于應物之處，無少差謬，而無適不然，則爲有以致其和矣。乃若土木之事、神仙之技、甲兵之釁，必絕而去之，懼其有以戾吾之中也；世俗之樂、鄭衛之音、萋菲之言，必放而遠之，懼其有以乖吾之和也。由
translation_en:
…ritual and music as empty formalities. What constitutes their practical application? Rooting them in the heart and expressing them in one’s own conduct; beginning within the palace apartments and extending them to the court; proceeding from the capital region to influence all under Heaven. What is meant by empty formalities? Being exacting in governing one’s ministers but lax concerning the ruler’s own person; applying them throughout the realm but failing to extend them to one’s own household; elaborately displaying the trappings of peace while neglecting the substance of governing through ritual and deference.
Thus it is said: “The fu and gui offering vessels, the zu stands and dou dishes, prescribed forms and ornamental patterns are the implements of ritual. Ascending and descending, moving above and below, turning about, and baring or covering the outer robe are the forms of ritual. Bells, drums, pipes, sounding stones, feather plumes, flutes, shields, and axes are the implements of music. Bending and stretching, bowing and raising the head, the marked positions of dancers, and their quick and slow movements are the forms of music.” It is also said: “Being centered and upright, without perversity, is the substance of ritual. Solemnity, reverence, respect, and obedience are the standards of ritual. Ordered relationships without trouble [?] are the essential character of music. Joy, delight, affection, and love are the functions of music.”
The substance of ritual and music consists entirely in the perfection of equilibrium and harmony. The perfection of equilibrium and harmony consists entirely in the virtue of one’s nature and feelings; and that virtue consists entirely in the work of making stillness primary and being watchful over oneself when alone. Thus the inner palace and the great court form a single whole; the vital energy of morning, daytime, and night proceeds from a single source. If one can truly gather oneself through vigilance and apprehension until one reaches utter stillness, without the slightest partiality or inclination, and maintains this without lapse, one will have the means to bring equilibrium to its fullest realization. If one refines oneself through watchfulness in solitude until, in responding to things, there is not the slightest error, and this holds wherever one goes, one will have the means to bring harmony to its fullest realization. As for construction projects, techniques for attaining immortality, and provocations to war, one must entirely renounce and remove them, fearing that they might disrupt one’s equilibrium. Worldly pleasures, the music of Zheng and Wei, and insinuating slander must be dismissed and kept at a distance, fearing that they might disturb one’s harmony. From…

title: 嘉靖二十年進士登科錄
text:
是吾之心正而天地之心亦正吾之氣順而
天地之氣亦順雖未施敬于民而民莫不敬
焉况夫禮以齊之乎雖未導和于民而民莫
不和焉况夫樂以宣之乎由是而教化以孚
人人有君子之行矣風俗以美比屋有可封
之俗矣災害以殄而雨暘之以時生養以遂
而禍亂之不作又由是而天地忻合陰陽相
得山出器車河出馬圖草木繁殖蟄蟲昭蘇
與夫諸福之祥四靈之物莫不畢至是謂大
順大化治之至也此聖神功化之極正
===
陛下之能事也苟或中和之效猶未能如先王之
盛則愚臣之言或亦未可以葑菲而遽棄也
臣狂瞽之見干冒
天威無任恐懼隕越之至臣謹對

不和焉況夫樂以宣之乎由是而敎化以孚

而禍亂之不作又由是而天地忻合陰陽相

與夫諸福之祥四靈之物莫不畢至是謂大
順大化治之至也此聖神功化之極正
===
陛下之能事也苟或少有之爻獲未能如先王之
盛則愚臣之言或亦未可以爲非而遽棄也
臣任贅之見干冒
天威無任恐懼隕越之至臣　謹對
punctuated:
是吾之心正，而天地之心亦正；吾之氣順，而天地之氣亦順。雖未施敬于民，而民莫不敬焉，况夫禮以齊之乎？雖未導和于民，而民莫不和焉，况夫樂以宣之乎？由是而教化以孚，人人有君子之行矣；風俗以美，比屋有可封之俗矣；災害以殄，而雨暘之以時；生養以遂，而禍亂之不作。又由是而天地忻合，陰陽相得，山出器車，河出馬圖，草木繁殖，蟄蟲昭蘇，與夫諸福之祥、四靈之物，莫不畢至。是謂大順大化，治之至也。此聖神功化之極，正陛下之能事也。苟或中和之效猶未能如先王之盛，則愚臣之言，或亦未可以葑菲而遽棄也。
臣狂瞽之見，干冒天威，無任恐懼隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
…Thus, when my heart is rectified, the heart of Heaven and Earth is likewise rectified; when my vital energy is harmonious, the vital energy of Heaven and Earth is likewise harmonious. Even before reverence is imparted to the people, none fails to be reverent—how much more so when ritual brings them into conformity! Even before the people are guided toward harmony, none fails to be harmonious—how much more so when music gives it expression! Through this, moral instruction wins their trust, and everyone conducts himself as a gentleman. Customs become good, and every household displays conduct worthy of receiving an enfeoffment. Calamities are extinguished, and rain and sunshine arrive in season; life and nurture flourish, and disasters and disorder do not arise. Through this, moreover, Heaven and Earth unite in delight, and yin and yang accord with one another. Mountains yield vessels and carriages, and the river yields the horse and its chart. Plants and trees multiply, and hibernating creatures awaken and revive. All auspicious signs of blessing and all four numinous creatures appear together. This is called supreme harmony and supreme transformation, the highest attainment of governance. This pinnacle of sagely and divine achievement and transforming influence is precisely what Your Majesty is capable of accomplishing. If, however, the effects of equilibrium and harmony have not yet attained the fullness achieved by the former kings, then perhaps these words of your foolish servant should not be hastily discarded as mere turnip and radish greens—that is, rejected for their humble source.
Your servant’s rash and unseeing opinions have offended against Your Heavenly Majesty. I am overcome with fear and dread, apprehensive in the extreme of falling into ruin. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.
